Sports.title: UEFA 'threaten to BOYCOTT the World Cup' over FIFA's proposal to sell stakes in the competition in a move that could make president Gianni Infantino millions
Sports.content:
UEFA 'threaten to BOYCOTT the World Cup' over FIFA's proposal to sell stakes in the competition in a move that could make president Gianni Infantino millions

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

European nations are to hold discussions over boycotting the World Cup after UEFA hit out at a leaked FIFA plan to sell stakes in the competition in a move that could make its president Gianni Infantino millions.

News broke in The Times on Tuesday afternoon that FIFA boss Infantino was considering selling parts of the tournament to private investors and forming a new company in a deal that could be worth around £15billion, which the governing body later confirmed in a hastily-issued statement.

The report added that Infantino could become the commissioner of that company once his role at FIFA ends in 2031, a highly lucrative position that estimates suggest could pay him more than $50million-a-year.

The bank JPMorgan is said to be handling the process and the Donald Trump administration is understood to have been consulted.

The proposal has already received widespread criticism from across football, with one source telling The Times it would be a 'nuclear bomb' for the sport and another arguing it would 'potentially be much worse than the European Super League'.

Now, according to Sky, UEFA members are set to hold an emergency meeting this week to discuss the possibility of skipping the competition and other details to oppose Infantino's ideas.

FIFA are reportedly planning to sell stakes in the World Cup in a hugely contentious move

UEFA launched a strongly worded statement slamming plans that 'crossed a line' (pictured - UEFA President Aleksander Ceferin)

That could mean the likes of World Cup holders Spain, as well as semi-finalists England and France, would no longer take part in the competition.

It is understood the English FA were completely unaware of the proposal before it was made public, and UEFA, which has been critical of FIFA and Infantino's actions in recent times, hit out at the plans almost immediately.

'This crosses a line that football's governing institutions should never cross,' they said in a statement. 'UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association.

'So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

'The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA's to sell.'

The potential boycott could come as early as next year, with the Women's World Cup set to take place in Brazil in the summer.

It's understood UEFA do have some pulling power, with UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin making it clear five years ago that European nations would not participate in a World Cup held every two years instead of the current four.

Infantino said: 'Our next stage of growth needs a structure built for it, one where the commercial side of the game operates as a focused, dedicated business, with its value shared more and better all around the world.

Joshua Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, was reported to be one of the potential investors

'Every FIFA Member Association should have an opportunity to seek a fair share of the available funding to shape its own future, deciding for itself rather than relying on others. This is about the democratisation of football worldwide.'

Former FIFA president Sepp Blatter condemned the governing body's reported plan.

'The close relationship between the FIFA President and the US President has reached a financial dimension that is deeply damaging football,' Blatter wrote on X.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham also hit out at FIFA on social media, writing: 'No one has the right to sell our game.'

'Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

'The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell.

'Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.'

If the move was to go ahead, the global football calendar would likely be affected.

For example, the Men's and Women's World Cup may be expanded or held more regularly than every four years, while the Club World Cup could face similar changes.

As part of the proposal, all 211 member associations would have stakes that would make up 20 per cent of the total company and be worth around $20million (£15million) each.

That is a larger figure than many of their annual revenues, and they would be given the option to sell them to raise funds.

FIFA would retain a majority stake in the new entity and private investors would be able to take on minority stakes.

FIFA is a not-for-profit organisation and enjoys tax-free status at its HQ in Switzerland.

For the most recent cycle of 2022-2026, their revenue is expected to be around $15billion (£11.3billion) – much of which came from this summer's World Cup – meaning this would provide a lucrative opportunity for individuals to be involved in.

The Times added that the blueprint for the potential selling of stakes has been discussed among senior FIFA figures and potential investors, which could include Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared – and they have signed non-disclosure agreements.

Some of those potential investors are understood to have even spoken internally about 'buying FIFA'.

Infantino's proposed new role could be extremely lucrative. Figures close to the plan are said to see it on a par with the NFL, whose commissioner Roger Goodell earns about $64million a year.

The reports come at a time when Infantino is already under fire for a variety of reasons following the World Cup.

This includes the US visa restrictions that affected supporters and officials from many countries, the extremely high prices of tickets and Infantino's links with Trump, which came to a head after Folarin Balogun's red card was suspended following a phone call by the US President to the Swiss administrator.

When contacted for comment, FIFA confirmed plans to launch a new body called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which they described as a 'controlled subsidiary consolidating FIFA's commercial and event operations'.

They added that 'FIFA would retain sole control of FFE and exclusive authority over football governance, competitions, match calendar, and all regulatory and sporting decisions,' and claimed the move would increase the funding available to all 211 member associations.

Daily Mail Sport also contacted the White House for comment.

Sports.title: Andy Burnham delivers passionate World Cup defence in face of FIFA plan to SELL competition
Sports.content:
Andy Burnham delivers passionate World Cup defence in face of FIFA plan to SELL competition

FIFA have been widely criticised for their plan to auction off a share in the World Cup to private investors and Prime Minister Andy Burnham has now had his say in a strong statement

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has hit back at FIFA's plan (Image: Getty Images)

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has torn into FIFA for being ‘sell outs’ amid their plan to sell a share of the World Cup.

‌



World football’s governing body has unveiled a new plan to auction off a share in the competition to foreign investors - a plot that has been met with widespread criticism.

‌



Among the critics is UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Talking to social media, he wrote: “Let me say this very directly. Football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine.

‌



“The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone's to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out. Football belongs to the fans. It always has, and it always will.”

UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words READ MORE :

PM Burnham is not the only one to have hit out in the midst of FIFA's latest plan. European football's governing body UEFA have also had their say.

A statement read: “This crosses a line that football’s governing institutions should never cross.

‌



“UEFA takes it extremely seriously. So should every National Football Association. So should every stakeholder: leagues, clubs, players, supporters, governments and everyone who cares about the future of the game.

“The soul and governance of football are not assets to trade - especially with zero transparency as to who gains financially. None of us are the owners of football. It is not FIFA’s to sell.”

Meanwhile, the Football Supporters' Association (FSA) released a scathing assesment. A statement on Tuesday read: “Many supporters came home from the World Cup believing FIFA couldn’t do much more to ruin everything we love about football’s greatest tournament. Less than two weeks after the final ball was kicked, they’ve shown they can always find a new low.

‌



View 2 Images Trump's administration have already been told about FIFA's plan (Image: Getty Images)

“Like so many across the game, we are furious. We will examine the detail as it emerges, but we will do everything in our power as fans to fight back against the long line of decisions made that seriously threaten the future of football for short-term commercial gain.

“This cannot become another step in Gianni Infantino’s attempt to reshape football without regard for supporters or the wider game. We fully support UEFA’s statement. Every governing body, national association, league, club, supporter and stakeholder now has a responsibility to stand together and protect the future of our game.”

‌



FIFA have already issued their official plan. They confirmed that they intend to increase funding to over $10 billion (£7.49 billion). That funding would then be available to all 211 associations that are members of FIFA.

FIFA would remain as majority stakeholders of the World Cup, with private investors buying 20 to 30 per cent, and the member organisations receiving a small stake totalling 20 per cent.

Sports.title: Argentine Premier League stars 'employ private security' after heated England win
Sports.content:
Argentine Premier League stars 'employ private security' after heated England win

Argentina reached the 2026 World Cup final with a controversial victory against England and it appears that some stars playing in the Premier League have stepped up their security measures in the aftermath

View 2 Images Alexis Mac Allister after Argentina's World Cup final defeat (Image: Getty Images)

Lisandro Martinez and Alexis Mac Allister decided to bolster their home security in the aftermath of Argentina’s dramatic World Cup win against England. The South American nation reached the final earlier this month with a late, turnaround victory against the Three Lions.

‌



Anthony Gordon had given Thomas Tuchel ’s men the lead, only for goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez to turn the game on its head. Argentina players were criticised in the aftermath for celebrating with a banner declaring that the Falkland Islands were Argentinian, while their physical approach to the game was also a sticking point.

‌



And it appears that some of the players currently playing in the Premier League stepped up their security at their houses in the face of potential backlash. According to The Sun, both Mac Allister and Martinez employed private security firms to patrol their houses shortly after Argentina’s win.

‌



Those teams were present for two days following the game, albeit no attempts were made to vandalise either of the players’ properties. Manchester United are not thought to have had any involvement in Martinez’s arrangement for more security.

UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words READ MORE :

Argentina eventually lost the World Cup final against Spain - Ferran Torres’ extra-time strike securing victory for the European side.

Speaking after the World Cup final, Liverpool midfielder Mac Allister slammed rival fans for their responses. He said: "I have mixed feelings. It makes me a little angry because they have no basis for generating that hatred.

‌



“They say we're arrogant but maybe it says more about the people who say those things than about us. We have always been respectful to our opponents."

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez also stepped up security at his UK home (Image: Getty Images)

Taking to social media, he added: "Let's cry, because we're Argentinians and we always want to win. But after crying, let's get up, unite, and keep going, because this isn't over. And these past few days, my mum reminded me of a popular saying: 'If there's a rematch, don't be afraid.'

‌



"Finally, my eternal gratitude to our families, friends, those who do the silent work for this national team, and everyone who supports us throughout the year, in good times and bad. You are a huge part of who we are.

"Thank you to all Argentinians for every message of love and support. You don't know how important you are on this journey. And thank you also to those from other countries who send us messages mocking or rejoicing in our pain.

"Without meaning to, you help us feel more and more proud to be Argentinian every day. THANK YOU ARGENTINA!"

Sports.title: Vinicus Jr set to STAY at Real Madrid despite Arsenal interest as Jose Mourinho pulls rank
Sports.content:
Vinicus Jr set to STAY at Real Madrid despite Arsenal interest as Jose Mourinho pulls rank

Arsenal have been linked with a move for Real Madrid forward Vinicius Jr, but the Brazilian is reportedly set to stay at the Bernabeu

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr will reportedly remain at Real Madrid amid interest from Arsenal. (Image: Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has intervened and Arsenal target Vinicius Junior will not leave the club, according to reports. Sky Sports have claimed that the former Chelsea and Manchester United manager is keen to keep the Brazilian in the Spanish capital, scuppering Mikel Arteta's hopes of a landmark signing.

‌



The forward is into the last 12 months of his deal at the Bernabeu and uncertainty had been cast over his future at Madrid with the prospect of losing him on a free transfer. However, Mourinho has stepped in and Los Blancos will reportedly not sanction a sale while there is confidence that he will sign a new deal with the club.

‌



The Gunners had shown a genuine willingness to fund a move for the 26 year old after identifying the winger as a considerable upgrade on their current options, according to football.london.

‌



UEFA hit back at FIFA plan to SELL World Cup in bitter war of words READ MORE :

Arteta's side had been assessing the feasibility of pushing through a deal, with the Premier League-winning manager giving his blessing for the transfer to go ahead.

Arsenal had been on high alert regarding the prospect of snapping up Vinicius, with the two-time Champions League winner entering the final 12 months of his contract at the Bernabeu.

However, the Gunners will now be forced back to the drawing board, with Mourinho determined to keep his prized assets available as he prepares for his first season back at the helm.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

It is understood that Vinicius and the Spanish giants are poised to enter fresh discussions, with the Brazilian international fully expected to put pen to paper on a new long-term contract.

Club president Florentino Perez is reportedly central to the negotiations and has made no secret of his determination for the forward to stay. Real Madrid head into the upcoming season aiming to topple rivals Barcelona from the top spot, after Hansi Flick's side cruised to La Liga glory with relative ease.

‌



Despite falling short of domestic honours, Vinicius remained integral to Real Madrid's attacking play, contributing 22 goals and 14 assists across all competitions. BBC Sport revealed earlier this week that the forward was open to staying at the club but wished 'to feel loved' with his new contract reflecting his significance to the side.

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr celebrates winning the 2023/24 Champions League with Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images Europe)

Mourinho's team have been active this summer following the signings of Ibrahima Konate and Bernardo Silva on free transfers, while they secured Marc Cucurella and Denzel Dumfries from Chelsea and Inter Milan respectively.

‌



Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence against newly-promoted Coventry City on August 21 as they seek to successfully retain their top-flight trophy.

Christos Tzolis became the most recent summer acquisition after finalising his switch from Club Brugge. This summer's transfer window has proved a challenging market to navigate following the missed opportunities for Morgan Rogers and Jeremy Monga.

Chelsea and Manchester City moved swiftly to secure the two highly-regarded additions following Arsenal's public chase of the duo. Vinicius' standing could mean that any transaction for his services will surpass £100million.

Article continues below

Any transfer would almost certainly have implications for Gabriel Martinelli's future, with the club understood to be willing to entertain offers this summer.

Sports.title: Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton
Sports.content:
Village cricket rocked by cheating allegation after Saltburn's clash with Norton

An investigation has now been launched into Saltburn’s 2nd XI cricket match with Norton in Division Two of the North Yorkshire and South Durham League

View 2 Images A village cricket game is being investigated

Village cricket has been rocked by a cheating scandal after a fielder was accused of clicking his fingers to mimic the sound of the ball hitting the bat.

‌



Footage appears to show a slip fielder for Saltburn 2nd XI snapping his fingers just before his wicketkeeper takes a catch. The batter appears confused to be given out.

‌



After the clip circulated, people accused him of fooling the umpire into thinking the batter had edged the ball.

‌



Ben Mummery, who shared the footage on social media, said: "Click-gate has gone viral and I’m genuinely really happy it’s being exposed. Harshest possible punishment please. It’s not cricket."

England cricket icon says wife was left 'suicidal' over Azeem Rafiq racism storm READ MORE :

View 2 Images An investigation has been launched into Saltburn’s match with Norton after cheating allegations (Image: Saltburn CC)

‌



The incident happened in a match in the North Yorkshire and South Durham League (NYSDL) between Saltburn 2nd XI and Norton 2nd XI, while ­Saltburn were fielding.

League leaders Saltburn ended up winning by a huge margin of 159 runs at their home ground in North Yorkshire.

Rory Cotterill, who captained Middlesbrough CC’s 2nd XI in a 29-run defeat to Saltburn in June, has since claimed a similar situation occurred in that match. He shared a video online which allegedly showed the same player clicking his fingers.

Article continues below

The NYSDL confirmed it received a formal complaint regarding S­aturday’s game.

It said: “A full investigation has been initiated and until such time as the formal processes are complete no further comment will be made.”

Saltburn CC has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Man Utd handed Aurelien Tchouameni timeline hint amid Real Madrid agreement mystery
Sports.content:
Man Utd handed Aurelien Tchouameni timeline hint amid Real Madrid agreement mystery

Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni continues to be linked with a summer move to Manchester United as Michael Carrick looks to bolster his midfield options

View 2 Images Man Utd are interested in Real Madrid and France star Aurelien Tchouameni (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United could potentially sign Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni in August - if Rodri joins the Spanish giants by then. The French midfielder has reportedly signed a contract extension at Los Blancos, but the La Liga side are yet to confirm it, leading to hope at Old Trafford.

‌



The Red Devils are open to signing a third midfielder this summer after Casemiro's departure and Manuel Ugarte's serious injury during the recent World Cup. United have signed Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa so far, but Michael Carrick's squad lacks a specialist defensive midfielder.

‌



That has led to links with former Monaco star Tchouameni. It is understood that United have conducted background checks on the 26-year-old several months ago and are keen on a deal should he become available.

‌



Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Ruben Amorim admits to Man Utd mistakes and explains how sacking has changed him READ MORE :

And despite confusion over whether the No.8 has signed a contract extension at the Santiago Bernabeu, Real have been linked with a big-money move for Manchester City star Rodri and may need to drum up funds.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Spanish giants have stepped up their interest in the 30-year-old, who is into the final year of his City contract. Rodri has been offered fresh terms by the Blues, but the deal remains unsigned, and his future this summer remains uncertain.

‌



The Spanish World Cup winner has undergone surgery and is expected to remain out of action for a few weeks. When back to full fitness though - Real could make their move and sign him.

View 2 Images Rodri could hold the key to Man Utd signing Tchouameni (Image: Getty Images)

That means United could then have an opening to acquire Tchouameni in mid-August. Carrick's men have until the summer transfer window closes on September 1 to sign him.

‌



At City, new Blues manager Enzo Maresca has insisted that Rodri would 'be back with us' and that he was not concerned by the transfer speculation surrounding his star midfielder.

He said: "We have to say that around big players there are always speculation. I'm not worried about that, it's normal.

"They won the World Cup and he was one of the best players.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso drops telling hint over Chelsea’s Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck transfers

Chelsea have been linked with moves for veteran Premier League stars Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck and boss Xabi Alonso has spoken out on deals for the pair

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso took charge of his first Chelsea match on Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

Xabi Alonso has refused to confirm Chelsea are interested in signing Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson - but hinted that the Blues want to add more experience. The Blues have been linked with moves for the veteran stars over the past few days.

‌



Reports have suggested that Henderson, 36, will be allowed to leave Brentford on a free transfer just a year after moving to West London. It has also been suggested that Chelsea are already in talks with Brighton regarding a move for Welbeck.

‌



Asked about potential deals following Tuesday’s 6-4 victory against Western Sydney Wanderers, new Chelsea boss Alonso remained tight-lipped.

‌



He said: “No, I'm sure that from today until the last day of the transfer [window] there will be a lot of rumours, so to be commenting on all of them. It's going to be a hard task, but for sure we need proper balance in terms of qualities, in terms of positions, in terms of balance.

“We want to have a complete squad and we want to make a good team. For that we have an idea, we have a plan and let's see how we set it up until the start of the Premier League.”

Chelsea hoping to repeat Man Utd and Liverpool's inspired transfer deals with latest moves READ MORE :

Xabi Alonso left with easy transfer decision as Chelsea win Western Sydney Wanderers goalfest READ MORE :

Chelsea’s moves for Henderson and Welbeck are huge departures from their previous approach in the market. Having preferred to sign youth with promise in previous windows, the Londoners now appear to be prioritising experience.

‌



Chelsea have of course already been busy in the window this summer. Morgan Rogers arrived from Aston Villa for £117m earlier this summer, while Marco Palestra was signed from Atalanta.

Elsewhere, Geovany Quenda and Emmanuel Emegha arrived at Stamford Bridge on pre-agreed moves. The Blues have already earned considerable sums back, with Andrey Santos and Marc Cucurella having joined Manchester United and Real Madrid respectively.

View 2 Images Chelsea are interested in signing Jordan Henderson (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Tyrique George has signed permanently for Everton following last season’s loan spell, while Alejandro Garnacho has been allowed to move to Aston Villa on loan. Another star who could leave before the end of the transfer window is striker Liam Delap.

The 23-year-old endured a difficult debut season with Chelsea, having netted on just three occasions. On the striker, Alonso added: “Every player that is involved is doing well, Liam as well. It was 60 minutes when he had to battle hard against the centre-backs, a good few lays off, so he's doing well and preparing for the season.

“I see him in a good mood, in a good desire to get proper fitness, proper football feeling good, and he's doing well.”

Sports.title: Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy
Sports.content:
Glorious Goodwood tips: Wednesday's best bets for EVERY race from our top tipster Newsboy

Unmissable in-depth analysis of all eight races on the second day of the Festival which stages the week's signature race, the Sussex Stakes

View 6 Images Newsboy provides tips for Goodwood (Image: PA)

1.50 Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap: CANNES is entitled to a plea of mitigation following his Royal Ascot blowout and deserves another chance.

‌



A debut second to his stablemate James J Braddock at the Curragh last November, the son of Sea The Stars took the silver medal home from his return to action at Leopardstown in April, but went one better in handsome style at the Foxrock venue the following month.

‌



Joseph O’Brien then gave Cannes his handicap debut in the King George V Stakes punters bought into the plan - my selection went off the 7-2 market leader in a field of 19.

‌



Eastender Kaiya Fraser hoping to star on the big stage at Goodwood READ MORE :

His supporters were left out of pocket when Dylan Browne McMonagle’s mount returned in 14th place behind his Ryan Moore-partnered stablemate Enceladus - but there are excuses.

Despite the big field, the leaders didn’t go off at a breakneck pace and the race unfolded to favour those positioned nearer the front than the back, which is where Cannes found himself during the early stages.

The handicapper has left Cannes on an unchanged mark of 95 and that’s a rating that looks within range for a colt who has plenty more to offer, while the unstoppable form of his trainer’s team is another reason to be cheerful.

‌



Of the remainder, Hatteen , Infraad and, at bigger odds, Parisian Scholar are three-year-olds open to further progress who have a role to play.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 CANNES, 2 HATTEEN, 3 PARISIAN SCHOLAR

View 6 Images Karl Burke: trains Newsboy's tip (Image: PA)

‌



2.25 British Stallion Studs EBF Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes: WILD BLOSSOM is a two-year-old filly of significant promise who should make full use of this drop in class.

The daughter of Mehmas - dam Duchess Rose didn’t win but is a half-sister to Queen Elizabeth II Stakes hero Bayside Boy - cost 300,000 guineas at the breeze-up sales in April before being sent to join Karl Burke by owners Wathnan Racing.

Making her racecourse debut in a four-runner novice stakes for fillies over five furlongs at Carlisle the following month, Wild Blossom could hardly have been more impressive, sent to the front by James Doyle inside the two-furlong pole before careering away to humble Crownbreaker by 10 lengths.

‌



Sent off at 7-1 for the Group 2 Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot, my selection completed in 10th, beaten just over four lengths, behind winner Victorious, with four of today’s opponents in behind.

But that effort merits an upgrade as subsequent events at the meeting showed the far side, where Wild Blossom finished third in a group of 11, was at a disadvantage to the stands’ rail. With her sights lowered to conditions-stakes level, Wild Blossom is expected to get back to winning ways before returning to Group company.

Fast Track, 14th in the Queen Mary before a runaway success at Beverley, is a strong candidate for the podium, along with Weatherbys Super Sprint winner Zigazig Ah and Hidden Gift.

‌



NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 WILD BLOSSOM, 2 FAST TRACK, 3 HIDDEN GIFT

View 6 Images Simon Crisford: trains Newsboy's pick with son Ed

5.00 Rolls-Royce Oak Tree Stakes - ZANTHOS hasn’t yet reproduced the form of her two-year-old season - but there’s no time like the present.

‌



Roll the clock back to the autumn of 2025 and the daughter of Sioux Nation, trained in tandem by Simon and Ed Crisford, was proving herself in a higher grade than the company she’s keeping today.

A debut winner at Newmarket in August, Zanthos was unexpectedly beaten at odds of 4-11 at Leicester a month later. But she left that form well behind when outpointing The Prettiest Star by half a length for the Group 2 Rockfel Stakes back at Newmarket on her final start as a juvenile. It’s no calumny against Zanthos to say things haven’t worked out so far this term.

Returning in Longchamp’s Poule d’Essai des Pouliches in May, Oisín Murphy’s partner finished ninth of 15 behind Diamond Necklace and, stepping back from a mile to six furlongs, she came back 16th of 22 in the Group 1 Commonwealth Cup at Royal Ascot won by Venetian Sun.

‌



But seven furlongs on fast ground are the conditions that have shown Zanthos, fitted with a tongue strap, in her best light and the drop to Group 3 level will help her bid to bounce back. Flora Of Bermuda carries a penalty for her success in York’s Group 3 Summer Stakes 19 days ago but is feared most, ahead of Planet Seeker and Radiant Beauty.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ZANTHOS, 2 FLORA OF BERMUDA, 3 PLANET SEEKER

View 6 Images Kaiya Fraser: won on Adonius at Chester (Image: PA)

‌



3.35 Veuve Clicquot Molecomb Stakes: ADONIUS is the choice to give Co Durham trainer Rebecca Menzies a winner at Goodwood with her first-ever runner at the track.

The son of Soldier’s Call is already the best horse dual-purpose trainer Menzies has handled on the Flat - and is still a long way from the bottom of the barrel.

Reputed to be full of spirit during his pre-training days, Adonius was gelded prior to his debut at Musselburgh at the beginning of April but channelled his energies in the right direction to score by seven lengths.

‌



Adonius had just a neck to spare over Rlasthope under a penalty in East Lothian eight days later but did enough to earn a trip to Chester’s May fixture, where he contested the curtain-raising Lily Agnes EBF Conditions Stakes.

Again in front from flagfall under Kaiya Fraser, my selection took his record to 3-3 with a length-and-a-quarter dismissal of Hickory Lad.

Menzies resisted the temptation to go to Royal Ascot with Adonius, whose train-to-catch way of doing things will be well suited to the South Downs as he moves up to Group 3 level, and her patience can yield its reward.

‌



Pershaada, Ruler’s Pride and El Floridita were all beaten in different races at the royal meeting but warrant respect, all the same.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 ADONIUS, 2 PERSHAADA, 3 EL FLORIDITA

View 6 Images Bow Echo (right) wins by a short head from Gstaad (Image: Mike Egerton/PA Wire)

‌



4.10 Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes: BOW ECHO has yet to taste defeat and is expected to take the score in his private battle with Gstaad to 3-0.

A perfect 3-3 as a two-year-old - he won a Newbury maiden, Haydock Park’s Listed Ascendant Stakes and the Group 2 Royal Lodge Stakes at Newmarket - the Night Of Thunder colt went into his winter quarters as one of the leading candidates for the 2,000 Guineas.

Bow Echo was an uneasy 9-2 chance on the big day, despite one upbeat bulletin after another from trainer George Boughey in the lead-up to the Rowley Mile test on the first Saturday in May.

‌



In the event, Billy Loughnane’s partner defied the market drift, coming from the back of the field to lead at the furlong pole and holding Gstaad by two and three-quarter lengths at the line, the pair a whopping eight lengths clear of third home Distant Storm.

Bow Echo went off at 5-6 to confirm that superiority over his Aidan O’Brien-trained rival in the St James’s Palace Stakes and did so - but only by a short head.

The result suggests that the momentum is with Gstaad, but Bow Echo tended to over-race after being leant on by the runner-up leaving the stalls yet demonstrated another facet to his game in being able to win ugly.

‌



It’s not hard to share Boughey’s view that Goodwood’s contours will play to Bow Echo’s strengths and he receives the vote to remain unbeaten.

Ten Bob Tony and Opera Ballo, first and third in the Queen Anne Stakes at the royal meeting, are taken to duke it out for the final place on the podium with the returning Zavateri and the top-class if quirky Never So Brave.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 BOW ECHO, 2 GSTAAD, 3 OPERA BALLO

‌

Don't miss out! Pick up your paper from Tuesday July 28 until Saturday August 1, 2026.

5.00 Coral Charlton Handicap: UNDER THE TWILIGHT was narrowly denied at this meeting 12 months ago but compensation is at hand.

The Michael Blake-trained mare went under by a neck to Dubai Treasure in the handicap for fillies and mares over course and distance, having scored at Windsor on her previous start. Under The Twilight then met with defeat on her next 10 starts but was back in business on Thameside 16 days ago.

‌



Sent off at 6-1 in a field of 12, Harry Davies’ mount came from the rear of the field to beat Amazonian Dream, who went one better at the track a week later, by a length and a half.

That success was gained from a British Horseracing Authority rating of 73 and Under The Twilight is 5lb higher in the handicap today.

But even that revised figure of 78 is 4lb beneath the mark from which she suffered last year’s near-miss, so the weights and measures point to another bold show.

‌



In a wide-open affair, Velvet Rhythm, French Affair, Lipsink and Calling A Star just four horses who merit a second glance.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 UNDER THE TWILIGHT, 2 VELVET RHYTHM, 3 CALLING A STAR

View 6 Images James Owen (second right) trains Newsboy's pick (Image: PA)

‌



5.40 HKJC World Pool Handicap: GOLDMOYNE has been a gold mine for punters since joining James Owen and another good run is on the cards.

The ex-Irish six-year-old son of Galileo Gold has won six of his 19 outings for the Newmarket trainer, the most recent success coming on Polytrack at Lingfield Park in March.

Goldmoyne has made the frame in five of his seven races since then, but that doesn’t mean the British Horseracing Authority handicapper has caught up.

‌



Two starts ago, my selection ran down the centre of the course to finish second to Royal Zabeel at Newmarket, where the winner was favoured by being stationed towards the far side. And his third, beaten two heads, behind Northern Express at York 19 days ago was another fine effort against a course specialist who was cashing in on a falling mark.

Hardly a day goes by without Owen saddling a winner, and jockey Mason Paetel’s 5lb claim is another plus. Bobby Bennu, Crimson Spirit and Zarathos are at the top of a long shortlist.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan

Semi-final: Italy vs Northern Ireland

Semi-final: Wales vs Bosnia and Herzegovina

Final: Wales/Bosnia and Herzegovina vs Italy/Northern Ireland - Tuesday, 7.45pm kick-off

Play-off Path B:
