World.title: Conflict shift
World.content:
Superintendent Mark Harris, commanding officer for the St Andrew Central Police Division, speaks about the division’s changing crime landscape during an episode of the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s Force4Good podcast. x

THE St Andrew Central Police Division, which is the commercial heartbeat of the Corporate Area, where thousands of Jamaicans live and work daily, is confronting a changing crime landscape, with police saying interpersonal and domestic conflicts have become a greater concern than organised gang violence.

Commanding officer for the St Andrew Central Police Division Superintendent Mark Harris said the division has largely brought organised gang activity under control, but is now grappling with murders arising from personal disputes, many of which occur without warning and in communities not traditionally associated with violent crime. He said this shift has presented a more complex policing challenge because, unlike gang conflicts, interpersonal disputes are far less predictable.

Speaking on the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s (JCF) Force4Good podcast, Harris said the division recorded the largest reduction in murders across the Jamaica Constabulary Force last year and even went an entire month without a murder this February. However, he noted that while gang-related killings have declined significantly, police are increasingly being challenged by crimes rooted in personal and domestic disputes.

“Last year, I had gang issues, [but] this year, we don’t have a gang issue, we have criminals committing crimes, but it’s not associated with gangs, like 2024 and part of 2025, and believe it or not, gang conflict is easier to police than the interpersonal and the domestic issues,” he noted.

The St Andrew Central Police Division encompasses some of Jamaica’s busiest commercial, educational and transport hubs, including Half-Way-Tree, New Kingston, Cross Roads and Papine. It is also responsible for policing major national events, entertainment activities and sporting fixtures that are often held at the National Stadium, making it one of the JCF’s most demanding divisions.

The division also includes communities such as August Town and Nannyville, both of which have experienced persistent gang activity and periodic security operations over the years. August Town was placed under a Zone of Special Operations in 2020 following years of deadly gang violence, while Nannyville has repeatedly featured in anti-gang and anti-gun operations as police sought to dismantle organised criminal networks operating across Kingston and St Andrew.

Despite that history, Harris said the division’s greatest challenge is no longer organised gangs but the rise in deadly interpersonal conflicts.

“We know where the gangs are and where they operate and who they’re in conflict with, and we put police right there…but for the interpersonal things, even in Jack’s Hill we have murders [and] that is not normally a place where we have murders… and these are interpersonal, rather than gang conflict,” he explained.

He said the division is relying not only on intelligence-led operations but also stronger community partnerships to prevent personal disputes from escalating into violence.

“We go out there and do the hard policing, we still have our community engagement. We had to do those meetings at the Transport Centre to speak to students and parents and stakeholders,” Harris noted.

Meanwhile, Area Four Commander Assistant Commissioner of Police Michael Phipps said St Andrew Central remains critical to crime management across Kingston and St Andrew because of its concentration of commercial activity, major institutions and daily commuter traffic.

He noted that the division has also experienced a significant number of fatal attacks involving weapons other than firearms, reflecting the growing challenge posed by interpersonal violence.

“I can tell you here and now that St Andrew Central has had a very high number of murders resulting from the use of knives and other blunt-force trauma injuries that have resulted in death. So we see St Andrew Central as one of the most important divisions if we are to maintain control of crime across Area Four,” Phipps said.

World.title: Upper St Andrew residents ready to protest
World.content:
The residents of Kingston 8 claim that a lot of the problems they face stem from an increase in large real estate projects in the area, as when projects are being executed, roads are dug up and not repaired properly. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

SOME residents of upper St Andrew have threatened to take up placards to protest poor road infrastructure and unrestricted real estate developments, as they say they are tired of their cries falling on deaf ears.

The Jamaica Observer was taken on a tour of Waterworks Road and adjoining thoroughfares in Kingston 8, starting from the Manor Park area, where various roadways that were recently patched have already started disintegrating.

The residents claim that a lot of the problems they face stem from an increase in large real estate projects in the area, as when projects are being executed, roads are dug up and not repaired properly. They also suspect that unregulated construction is a main factor in roads being damaged frequently even after being fixed.

“We are planning a protest, if nothing happens,” one resident threatened.

That resident, who withheld his name, pointed to a spot where water was spouting through a break in the asphalt on Waterworks Road. “They don’t use shingles or anything like that when they are fixing the roads, so the road is being eaten out from underneath,” he said.

As it relates to apartment projects being undertaken in the area, the resident said the road infrastructure can’t support the developments.

Pointing to premises on Waterworks Road where heavy-duty trucks used in construction were parked, the resident said the community has no idea what the plans for the location are, and is opposed to any more major construction projects at this time. Attempts have been made by members of the community to acquire information from the authorities about the developers’ plans, but they have hit a roadblock, having been told by authorities that they can get a copy of the documents in 60 days. However, this time frame poses a problem for the residents who said they are aware that under the law, they have a limited period in which to file an objection to any proposed construction projects.

In a letter recently penned by residents, which the

Observer saw, the residents said, “For nearly two years, residents of Broadway Close, Broadway Road, Sharrow Drive, and Waterworks Road in Kingston 8 have endured a slow-motion disaster. A developer dug up their roads to lay sewer pipes, left the reinstatement in a dangerously substandard condition, and vanished — while the authorities responsible for enforcing the law have failed to act. The result is that a car recently hit a sinkhole in a patched section and got stuck. Inferior patching work has crumbled under the weight of daily traffic. And residents are left asking a question that echoes across Jamaica: why are the laws on the books not being enforced?”

It continued: “The Parochial Roads Act gives the Kingston and St Andrew Municipal Corporation (KSAMC) clear and unequivocal authority over parochial roads like Broadway Road and Waterworks Road. It requires any developer digging up a public road to obtain a road-opening permit and provide a refundable security deposit — money held by the KSAMC to ensure that if the developer fails to properly restore the road, the corporation can do the job using those funds,” the letter stated.

“…On Broadway Road and Waterworks Road, the developer dug up the roads, laid pipes, and left behind inferior patching that has deteriorated into sinkholes and dangerous driving conditions. The KSAMC’s preliminary finding, confirmed by Member of Parliament for the area Delano Seiveright, is clear.

“But where is the accountability? If [a security deposit] was obtained [from the developer], why hasn’t it been used to fix the roads? If none was obtained, why was the developer allowed to dig up public roads without providing the required guarantee?“

Seiveright, meanwhile, said he shared the frustration of residents, stating that their concerns are legitimate and that he has been lobbying on their behalf for a remedy.

“It is important to note that the Waterworks issue pre-dates my election as Member of Parliament [for St Andrew North Central],“ he pointed out. ”Since taking office, I have met repeatedly with officials at the highest levels of the Ministry of Water, the National Water Commission (NWC), KSAMC, and the National Environment and Planning Agency, carried out several site visits and technical walk-throughs, and spoken directly with many affected residents. I also escalated the matter to Minister [of Water] Matthew Samuda.“

He said the situation in Waterworks centres on corrective works following a private developer’s sewer project in the area. He added that while the developer is at the heart of this debacle, he is pleased that KSAMC and the NWC are now working assiduously to deliver a proper resolution.

Seiveright said his advocacy has also helped to prompt a broader review of how these projects are supervised, with stronger oversight and policy improvements now being actively pursued.

“I am aware of similar issues in other communities. More broadly, residents have raised concerns about overdevelopment, infrastructure capacity and protecting community character. I share those concerns. Development must be responsible, properly planned and supported by adequate infrastructure. I have consistently conveyed residents’ views to the relevant authorities and have encouraged stronger community organisation,“ he explained.

“The Orange Grove/Bridgemount Citizens’ Association is an excellent example of the kind of united, constructive leadership that helps communities achieve results. I will continue to press vigorously for better communication with residents, stronger enforcement where necessary, and practical solutions that protect both our communities and their quality of life,” he said.

World.title: Saint International’s Fashion Face of the Caribbean set for August 29
World.content:
From left: Deiwight Peters, founder, CEO of Saint International; model Kai Newman; Member of Parliament for St Andrew Eastern and Minister of Finance Fayval Williams, and Saint International model Carolyn Sangster.Samuel Edie

For 26 years Saint International has been the leading model agency across the region, unearthing new talent each year who have gone on to achieve success on the international fashion scene.

A new set of model hopefuls are poised for international success after more than 30 were selected on Sunday, July 26 during a Saint International Community Model Search, which took place at Jamaica College.

This was the fifth model search to have taken place this year and, according to Saint International boss Deiwight Peters, this one was the biggest thus far.

“This model search is the last in the series, and we’ve had five so far. I do believe this was the biggest one; not only in terms of the size of the turnout, but certainly the faces that turned out, they were remarkable. I do feel strongly that on August 29, when we have the finals of the Fashion Face of the Caribbean competition (for both male and female), several of these new discoveries will go on to bigger things,” Peters told the Jamaica Observer shortly after the model search ended.

“We have several top agencies who will be coming in for the event, who are representing the major fashion markets in New York, London, Milan, Paris, Germany, and even Spain and they are just excited to be coming to Jamaica,” shared Peters.

Member of Parliament for St Andrew Eastern and Minister of Finance and the Public Service Fayval Williams, who was in attendance at the model search, heaped praises on Peters.

“Well, I was impressed to see the young people come out for the model search because I know there is still talent all over Jamaica. Deiwight is a very reputable person, his agency has an impressive track record, and I have no doubt that several of these model hopefuls here today will become stars of tomorrow under Deiwight’s guidance,” Williams told the Observer.

Peters shared that the minister’s presence validated the work that the agency has been doing over the years.

“I think that her turning up validated what we do and the purpose of the model search. She knows the success stories of Saint International. A big thank you to the Jamaica College family for hosting us, Mr Wayne Robinson, the principal, and the team,” he said.

Kai Newman, one of Saint International’s successful models, was in attendance at the model search to encourage the newbies.

“I just flew back to Jamaica so I said why not come here and meet some of the future stars and give them some advice, a little inspiration, and motivation. I just want them to believe in Deiwight, believe in Saint International, and to just be their authentic self,” Newman, who was discovered by Peters the age of 14 while walking on the street.

Newman has walked for designers including Burberry, Tommy Hilfiger, Chanel, Gucci, Calvin Klein, Prada, Bottega, among others.

Speaking on the Fashion Face of the Caribbean competition in August, Peters shared that more than 150 models from Jamaica, Canada, United States, Europe, several Caribbean countries including Guyana, will participate.

“We have roughly 150 models who will be participating in the Fashion Face of the Caribbean and they are coming from all over the world. It’s going to be awesome,” he said.

World.title: ‘Thrilled’ 76ers confirm James signing, eye NBA title run
World.content:
Lebron James Photo: AFP

NEW YORK, United States (AFP) — LeBron James has signed a contract to play for the Philadelphia 76ers, the team announced Monday, with managing owner Josh Harris “thrilled” about chances for their first NBA title since 1983.

James announced on Friday he would play for the Sixers on a two-year deal worth US$8 million, ending a weeks-long mystery over the 41-year-old superstar’s future, but the 76ers had no comment throughout the weekend.

“I am thrilled to welcome LeBron James to the Philadelphia 76ers,” ownership managing partner Harris said in a statement. “One of the greatest players in NBA history and one of the best athletes ever, his accomplishments are iconic.”

James, the NBA’s all-time scoring leader set to begin his record 24th campaign in October, is a four-time NBA champion and four-time NBA Most Valuable Player.

After winning two titles with Miami, another with hometown club Cleveland and his most recent with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020, James could become the first NBA player to win crowns with four different teams.

James, a three-time Olympic champion and 22-time NBA All-Star, joins a Sixers roster filled with NBA stars in hopes of bringing Philadelphia an NBA title for the first time since Julius Erving led the club to the crown 43 years ago.

“I cannot wait to see LeBron alongside Jaylen Brown, VJ Edgecombe, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and our talented roster as we work to deliver a championship for Philly,” Harris said.

“To LeBron and his family: we are grateful you chose the 76ers, and look forward to this next chapter of your legendary career. Welcome to the 76ers!”

James has career averages of 26.8 points, 7.5 rebounds, 7.4 assists and 1.5 steals over 1,622 games.

Philadelphia 76ers president of basketball operations Mike Gansey, an Ohio high school rival of James on the court, expects the legend will boost the club and the community.

“There’s no doubt LeBron is one of the greatest players to ever play the game of basketball and there are no words to measure the impact he’ll have on this organisation,” Gansey said.

“I’ve had the pleasure of knowing LeBron since high school and have seen the high-level impact he has produced at every stop of his basketball journey. He is a consummate professional, the ultimate competitor, and a tireless worker.

“But he’s also an incredible person with natural leadership traits, a family man, and someone who possesses unwavering commitment to community and those around him. We couldn’t be happier that he’s officially here.”

The 76ers posted a photo on social media of a James jersey, keeping his tradition number 23 with his new club, hanging in a locker with a crown on a shelf inside it, a nod toward “King James” being with the Sixers.

James has taken teams into the NBA play-offs 19 times, matching a league record, with post-season averages of 28.2 points, 8.9 rebounds, 7.2 assists, 1.7 steals and 1.0 blocked shots over 302 games.

In June, James announced he was leaving the Lakers and numerous clubs were seen as contenders to become his new home, including Miami, Cleveland, Golden State and Minnesota as well as the 76ers.

Philadelphia swung a deal with Boston three weeks ago for Brown, sending Paul George to the Celtics, and together with centre Embiid and top guards Maxey and Edgecombe they provided a line-up too good for James to pass up in his quest for a fifth NBA title.

“I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energise a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time,” James posted on X Friday.

World.title: DOUBLE JOY!
World.content:
DEMARIO Prince says a talk with his coach after the first round got his mind back where it was supposed to be, leading him to win the gold medal in the 110m hurdles on Monday’s first day of track and field at the Commonwealth Games at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow, Scotland.

Jamaica won two gold medals on the day as, minutes before Prince’s run, Romaine Beckford won the men’s high jump. Beckford’s leap to clear 2.25m brought Jamaica’s second gold in the event at the games and first in 68 years.

Prince, the fourth-straight Jamaican and fifth in the last six editions to win the 110m gold medal, ran 13.17 seconds (0.4m/s) to claim his first major global medal.

Prince, who was fourth in the 60m hurdles at the World Athletics Indoor Championships in March, was delighted with the win. “This means a lot. You know, that was the aim coming into the Commonwealth Games. You know, just to get the gold medal, do it for myself, my family, and the fans. So yeah, I’m very, very pleased, very happy with the win,” Prince told the Jamaica Observer.

The sprint hurdler said he believes this is the start of good things to come.

“I feel like I can still give more and still wrap up more gold medals,” he said, noting that he had not been happy with his first round race in which he placed second.

“I was more confident going into the final, I just had to go back in the mindset to know that I can go out there and execute as I was not pleased with the prelims. I spoke to coach Ben (Dalton) and he told me not to worry about anything, he told me that I can do this. It is a regular thing for me to go out and execute and go get the medal for Jamaica,” Prince said.

England’s Samuel Bennett ran a personal best 13.30 for the silver medal and Milan Trajkvoc clocked a season’s best 12.32 to deliver Cyprus’ first medal in the event. Jamaica’s Jerome Campbell was sixth in 13.86.

Beckford, who was eighth in 2022 and failed to clear the first height at last year’s World Athletics Championships, became the first Jamaican man to win the event since 1958 when Ernle Haisley set a then Commonwealth Games record 2.06m to capture gold.

India’s Sarvesh Anil Kushare, who also cleared 2.25m, took the silver medal. England’s NCAA champion Kimani Jack was third with 2.20m.

Two-time World Indoor bronze medallist Raymond Richards just missed a medal, placing fourth also with 2.20m.

Jamaica will hope to add more medals today with athletes qualified for several finals, including in the men’s and women’s 100m.

Women’s high jump defending champion Lamara Distin, former men’s 400m world champion Antonio Watson and 800m national champion Navasky Anderson are among those set to their first entry at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.

Former national champion Rohan Watson advanced to Tuesday’s semi-final of the men’s 100m after he won his first round race in 10.13 (1.5m/s).

In the semi-final he is to be joined by Ackeem Blake who drew a bye.

Also advancing were the Ghanaian pair of Benjamin Azamati and Abdul-Rasheed Saminu, as well as Jeremiah Azu of Wales and Favour Ashe of Nigeria.

Both Jamaican entries in the female 100m, Jonielle Smith and Jodean Williams, both of whom had byes, will join the action in the semi-finals.

Former World Athletics champion Tajay Gayle led the qualifying for Wednesday’s final of the men’s long jump with 8.10m (0.1m/s). He is to be joined by Jordan Turner who had a wind-aided 7.84m (4.2m/s).

Gayle, who have won medals at the last two major global championships, had a wind-aided 7.73m (3.3m/s) and 7.40m (1.0m/s) before his big mark.

Turner was was third in his group, behind Indian Sreeshankar’s effort of 8.01m (2.0m/s) and Australian Christopher Mitrevski’s mark of 7.89m (1.8m/s).

National champion Kelly Ann Beckford (2:01.63 minutes) and Adelle Tracey (2:02.58) advanced to Wednesday’s semi-finals of the women’s 800m.

Beckford booked an automatic spot after placing third in her first-round heat behind pre-championships favourite Lillian Odira of Kenya who ran 2:01.05. Isabelle Boffey of Wales clocked 2:01.53.

Tracey advanced on time after she was fourth in her first round race, just outside the automatic qualifying places. Australia’s Sarah Billings won with 2:01.51, followed by Botswana’s Oratile Nowe (2:02.11) and Kenya’s Janet Jepkemoi (2:02.30).

Nayoka Clunis qualified for Tuesday’s women’s hammer throw final, her first major global final. She threw 64.84m in the third round, eighth best of the day.

Distin could be pushed hard in her title defence with the likes of the in-form Australian pair of Eleanor Patterson and Nicola Olyslagers, as well as former NCAA champion Temitope Simbiat Adeshina of Nigeria all ranked ahead of her going into the championships.

The Sweden-based Distin has had a season’s best 1.96m, set indoors in February and has cleared 1.94m outdoors.

Navasky Anderson will be hoping to get back to the final of the men’s 800m after he finished fifth four years ago in Birmingham, England.

Since shocking the track and field world with his gold medal in the men’s 400m in Hungary in 2023, Watson has been through some lean years, failing to get past the semis in Tokyo, Japan, last year. But he has been improving through this season.

Watson will be accompanied by Delano Kennedy and Zandrion Barnes as they seek places in the men’s 400m semi-finals.

Leah Anderson and Shana Kaye Anderson are to line up in the women’s 400m first round.

World.title: Wedding Content Creators
World.content:
A wedding content creator documents your day as it unfolds, using a smartphone to capture raw, candid moments.

Not long ago, every wedding media team consisted of a photographer and videographer. Today, there’s a new professional joining the line-up — the wedding content creator.

If you’ve spent any time on Instagram or TikTok, you’ve probably seen the rise of behind-the-scenes wedding clips, emotional first looks, candid bridal party moments, and beautifully edited reels appearing within hours of the celebration. That’s the work of a wedding content creator.

This person is responsible for capturing authentic, real-time moments throughout the day, usually using a smartphone. The focus isn’t producing a cinematic wedding film or a gallery of professionally edited images. Instead, the wedding content creator documents the experience as it unfolds, creating vertical videos, candid clips, and social-ready content that couples can relive and share almost immediately.

So how are they different from a videographer? A videographer tells the story of your wedding through carefully planned shots, professional cameras, audio equipment, lighting, and expert editing. The result is a timeless wedding film that beautifully documents your ceremony, speeches, and celebration.

A content creator, on the other hand, captures the moments in-between — the laughter while getting ready, your mother’s emotional reaction as she helps you into your dress, the bridesmaids dancing in the suite, your guests’ excitement before the ceremony, or your partner’s nervous smile just before walking down the aisle. These are often the unscripted moments that couples cherish most because they reflect how the day actually felt.

Each has its advantages. A videographer delivers polished, high-quality storytelling that you’ll treasure for decades. The downside is that editing takes time, so your finished film may not arrive for several weeks or even months.

A content creator provides immediate gratification. Many deliver raw footage within 24 hours and edited reels shortly after, allowing couples to relive their day while the emotions are still fresh. However, smartphone footage is not intended to replace the production quality of professional videography.

If your budget allows, having both is the ideal combination.

The videographer preserves your wedding as a timeless film, while the content creator documents the emotion, spontaneity, and behind-the-scenes memories that often never make it into the final edit. Together, they create a complete story — one that is beautifully produced and deeply personal.

If you must choose one, let your priorities guide the decision. If preserving your vows, speeches, and ceremony in cinematic quality is more important, invest in a professional videographer. If you value candid moments, quick delivery, and social-media-ready memories, a content creator may be the better fit.

Whichever you choose, remember that great wedding content isn’t about following trends or chasing viral moments. The best professionals take the time to understand your personalities, your priorities, and the atmosphere you want to create. They know when to step in for a memorable shot and, just as importantly, when to step back and quietly capture the genuine interactions unfolding around them.

Because the most meaningful wedding memories aren’t always the ones you planned. They’re the fleeting glances, unexpected laughter, happy tears, and quiet moments that happen in-between.

At the end of the day, strong wedding content isn’t simply about documenting what happened, it’s about preserving how your wedding day felt — and that’s a memory worth investing in.

World.title: The spectacular split in Poland’s right
World.content:
Poland’s once-dominant Law and Justice party has split, with former PM Mateusz Morawiecki breaking with longtime leader Jarosław Kaczyński and preparing to build a rival force on the right. Zoya Sheftalovich and Ian Wishart examine whether the rupture offers current PM Donald Tusk a lifeline ahead of the 2027 election — and what it means in Brussels, where Morawiecki leads the European Conservatives and Reformists party.

They also look at plans to close Belgium’s Charleroi Airport for several months in 2028, leaving more than 10 million annual passengers, thousands of workers and Ryanair up in the air.

Plus: As Montenegro moves closer to EU membership, Brussels prepares to add Montenegrin as the bloc’s 25th official language.

World.title: The French presidential candidate who wants to blow up the Franco-German engine
World.content:
Instead, Mélenchon wants France to strengthen ties with China as well as French-speaking countries in Africa, as well as South American countries. He sees the United States as an imperialist danger, while Germany — despite its turbulent relations with President Donald Trump — views the transatlantic relationship as paramount to its foreign policy. Mélenchon is opposed to Germany’s deeply held attachment to its free-market economic model and favors a planned economy instead.

Mélenchon is also critical of Germany’s rearmament and the continued presence of U.S. nuclear weapons on its soil, which he said: “raise serious security concerns for neighboring countries.” Berlin aims to become Europe’s predominant military power in the wake of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and American retrenchment from Europe.

Mélenchon’s 2015 book “Bismarck’s Herring,” subtitled “The German Poison,” was meant to be a response to the many politicians who at the time in France viewed Germany as a policy model thanks to its low unemployment and strong growth rates.

Mélenchon pointed to the poverty rate in Germany, which at that time was several points higher than in France, and low birth rates as examples of the model’s failures.

“My goal is to pierce through the veil of bliss surrounding so many commentators who are fascinated by Germany,” reads the book’s blurb. “A monster has been born right before our eyes — the child of deregulated finance and a country that has devoted itself to it, ravaged by the accelerated aging of its population.”

Parts of French media, even left-leaning outlet Libération, deemed the book excessively Germanophobic. In it, Mélenchon adopts a provocative tone and states that “political confrontation with German governments is one of the conditions for the liberation of peoples.”

World.title: As France burns, the far right sees an opening
World.content:
“All the proposals that we have been putting forward for years with Marine and Jordan [Bardella] … today we realize that those are the only ones that could have spared us these situations, from protecting us from wildfires to saving our children,” she said. “Current events, alas, prove us right.”

Whether that argument will gain traction remains uncertain. But National Rally may not need voters to see it as an authority on climate change; its opening lies instead in the declining credibility of the parties that have governed France — and a sense among some voters that the state is no longer capable of protecting them.

Recent research shared with POLITICO — based on four focus groups with former center and center-left voters who appeared unlikely to support those parties again — found repeated references to a country that was falling apart. Participants cited a series of recent crises, including the murder of an 11-year-old girl by a suspect previously known to police, as evidence that the government was failing to act.

Marine Le Pen and Jordan Bardella arrive to attend a ceremony in Nice, France on July 14, 2026. | Pool photo by Philippe Magoni via AFP/Getty Images

That frustration extends to climate preparedness. In a YouGov poll published this month, 74 percent of respondents said they were dissatisfied with Macron’s climate-adaptation policies.

“The National Rally mechanically benefits from its anti-system positioning whenever there is a news event that gives the impression, right or wrong, that successive governments have not taken effective action to address the difficulties faced by the French people,” said Mathieu Gallard, research director at Ipsos France, a polling firm.

The fires have burned more than 1,000 square kilometers across southwestern France since the start of the summer — an area roughly 10 times the size of Paris — and forced more than 200,000 people from their homes. Coming after an extreme heatwave left the countryside tinder-dry, they have already scorched nearly twice as much land as during the last devastating fire season in 2022.

World.title: What voters really think of Britain’s new PM
World.content:
While there are still as many as three years to go before the next general election is called, Burnham’s arrival in No. 10 Downing Street — on the initial showing at least — seems to have changed the picture dramatically. Several pollsters in recent days have given Labour a small lead over Reform for the first time since the spring of 2025.

The POLITICO Poll delves deeper into voters’ first impressions of the new prime minister.

More than half the public — 54 percent — watched Burnham’s first speech on the steps of Downing Street after becoming prime minister, in which he set out his initial priorities for the job — and they gave him rave reviews.

Majorities agreed that he set out a clear vision for the country, that he’ll do the things he promised, and that he understands the problems that people like them face. He delivered the speech without notes or a lectern and voters seem to have approved of his communication style: Most said he is a good public speaker and his speech made them “feel more hopeful about the future” — a potentially significant mood shift, especially as Burnham promised to “bring back hope.”

That seems to have helped the new prime minister to make inroads among Reform voters — some of whom are former Labour voters the party hopes to win back.

Some 60 percent of Reform voters who watched Burnham’s first speech said they thought he was “a good public speaker.” One in three trusted that he would “do the things he promised” and said his speech made them feel more hopeful about the future. An even higher number — 44 percent — said Burnham “understands the problems facing people like me.” That’s more than the 38 percent of Reform voters who saw the speech and thought Burnham did not understand their problems.

World.title: EU proposes Brexit reset tuition fees compromise
World.content:
The EU has been pushing for European students to pay domestic rate tuition fees when studying at British universities, as they did before Brexit.

At £9,790, these are significantly lower than the eye-watering international fees international students have to pay — which are sometimes as high as £60,000 a year for the most prestigious courses.

But London has been resistant to the idea because its university sector says it depends on the cash to balance its books.

The Russell Group of research-intensive universities says the change would cost £580 million — money that administrators are skeptical the British Treasury would stump up to bridge the gap.

But a new idea now doing the rounds in Brussels is a halfway house, the two people — an EU diplomat and an EU official, both, like others in this story, granted anonymity to speak frankly — said.

While the EU is still seeking a cut in fees, its students would be expected to cover their costs to institutions. The result would be paying fees higher than domestic British students, but lower than other international students, from whom universities make a profit.

World.title: Merz’s fresh start quickly falls apart
World.content:
No one is yet saying out loud that Merz should go. But if his party performs poorly in three state elections in September, the crisis will likely become much harder to contain.

The drama has so far unfolded in two acts. The first began on July 14, when BILD — which, like POLITICO, is owned by Axel Springer — reported that Jens Spahn, the conservatives’ parliamentary group leader, and his husband had become parents through a surrogate mother in the United States.

“This feeling can hardly be put into words,” the paper quoted him as saying. The complication was plain enough: Surrogacy is banned in Germany, and the CDU has long opposed it, as had Spahn.

Patrick Schnieder arrives to attend the weekly Cabinet meeting in Berlin on June 24, 2026. | Ralf Hirschberger/ AFP via Getty Images

Merz’s standing has deteriorated since he took office in May 2025, with his support among voters falling as the far-right Alternative for Germany has surged to the top of the polls. The surrogacy controversy intensified the unease within the CDU.

The second act of the crisis was meant, in Merz’s telling, to be a liberation and a fresh start. Spahn, a long-standing rival whom Merz had always eyed warily, was made to resign, and a broader shake-up was supposed to quickly follow — only for things to fly off the rails.

On Thursday, Transport Minister Patrick Schnieder learned that he was to be dismissed and immediately told his staff by text message. But the man Merz had lined up to replace him was not yet convinced to take the job and withdrew.

World.title: Skip the usual stays: These five hidden gem hotels deserve a spot on your holiday shortlist
World.content:
Looking for a getaway where the hotel is every bit as memorable as the destination itself?

 

Ranking guide La Liste has revealed the winners of its Discovery Gem Hotel Awards for 2026, recognising five little-known stays that are worth the booking.

Self-styled as "the world’s most selective guide for discerning gourmets and travellers”, La Liste compiles its rankings using 370 expert sources across 200 countries and 7,200 establishments to create its guide of the world’s top stays.

This year's Discovery Gem Hotel Awards feature just two European properties. Here are the five that made the cut.

Islas Secas Resort, Panama

This Panamanian private island resort sits in one of the most exclusive and secluded private island retreats in the Americas.

The hideaway of “casas” and “casitas", located in the country’s Gulf of David, Chiriquí Province, offers 14 bedrooms that can accommodate up to 20 guests. The residences, shaded by trees and cooled by the sea breeze, typically overlook sweeping views of the ocean.

Serving up seasonal, coastal flair, Islas Secas also caters to every diner.

“Dining at Islas Secas is flexible, and you get to choose where and when you dine,” the resort said, adding that guests can choose when and where they sample dishes – whether it's Panamanian barbecue or ocean-to-table dining.

Les Sources de Vougeot, Burgundy, France

Set in the heart of Burgundy, Les Sources de Vougeot occupies a 14th-century residence once inhabited by the Cîteaux Abbots.

Offering guests an insight into the “true essence” of the French region, the hotel has 49 keys, including Le Moulin, which can host two adults and features a private Nordic bath, terrace and private garden.

Unsurprisingly, the gastronomy concepts serve fine dining that showcases the region's dishes, through multi-course menus, starting at €90.

Beyond the dining table, Les Sources de Vougeot also offers insights into the heritage and craftsmanship behind local favourites, such as Dijon mustard, burgundy cheese, Dijon gingerbread and blackcurrant through workshops and guided tour visits to artisan producers.

Arctic Bath, Harads, Swedish Lapland

The only other European entry to make this year’s cut is a floating hotel and spa on the Lule River in Swedish Lapland.

Inspired by the region’s timber-floating heritage, the circular Arctic Bath hotel becomes a sight to be seen when it freezes into the river during the winters. The retreat includes 12 rooms and cabins, all designed with Scandinavian interiors and offering panoramic views of the surrounding landscape.

Its spa and wellness centre offers guests cold baths, sauna, hot pool and treatments, including clay, ayurveda, massage, scalp and mind, starting at 1,595 Swedish krona (€144.10).

During the winters, guests can also brave the cold on a husky tour, go dogsledding and enjoy other seasonal excursions.

The Six Bells Countryside Inn, New York, USA

Bringing a slice of the British countryside to the Big Apple with its design around the fictional English village of “Barrow's Green”, this boutique inn is a whimsical take on cottage-core, a digital subculture centred on a romanticised rural lifestyle.

With names such as Innkeeper's suite, Mildred's Plum and Double Duke, the hotel’s 11 rooms are part of the stay’s concept of being a “storybook you can sleep in”.

In contrast to the English theme, the restaurant and tavern is rooted in early American and traditional country cookery.

Gangtey Lodge, Bhutan

Overlooking the pristine Phobjikha Valley nature reserve in Bhutan, this luxury retreat places guests in the Himalaya’s most picturesque settings.

The property features 12 farmhouse suites, each kitted with hand-cut stone floors. The suites also have “bhukharis”, which are traditional wood-burning stoves, as well as free-standing English roll-top bathtubs set next to a panoramic, valley-facing window.

The Lodge's “5 Keys to Wellbeing” experience involves immersing guests in nature, wellness, spiritual experiences, learning about Bhutanese gastronomy and local culture and customs for physical and mental rejuvenation.

World.title: US intercepts Iranian attack and launches joint strikes with Saudi Arabia against Iran-backed militias in Iraq
World.content:
The US military said on Tuesday that it knocked down an Iranian missile barrage and worked with Saudi Arabia's forces to strike sites in Iraq that Tehran-backed militias have used to launch attacks in recent days, shattering a brief pause in fighting.

 

All Iranian missiles launched against American forces in the Middle East were intercepted, US Central Command said, adding that they “remain vigilant and at a high state of readiness.”

In announcing the strikes in Iraq, the US warned that further attacks on American troops or Saudi Arabia’s energy infrastructure risked additional action.

Iran launched its ballistic missile attack before US and Saudi forces carried out strikes in Iraq, according to an American official, who stressed that the two attacks were not connected.

“US and Saudi fighter aircraft struck multiple terrorist logistics and weapons sites across eastern Iraq in a strong response to over 30 IRGC-directed aerial drone attacks in the last 72 hours,” the US Central Command said in a statement following its joint operation.

It said the Revolutionary Guard “and its terrorist proxies must cease these attacks to avoid further US military response.”

The Saudi Defence Ministry acknowledged the strikes in a post on X, warning that “the Kingdom emphasises that it does not seek escalation but will respond to any aggression it faces.”

It comes after Riyadh said on Tuesday that it had shot down drones fired by Iran-backed militias in Iraq for a second day.

The kingdom's Defence Ministry said air defences intercepted and destroyed several drones that had tried to target petroleum facilities in the nation's eastern region.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered security agencies to investigate after Riyadh alleged a similar attack on Monday. Baghdad said it is committed to “preventing Iraqi territory from being used as a route or launching point for any attack targeting brotherly or friendly countries.”

Iraqi militias have denied any role in the drone attacks. The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, an umbrella group of Iran-backed armed groups, called the Saudi claims “fabrications" and implied that Monday's attacks were carried out by the Houthis, who had themselves claimed to have attacked Saudi oil facilities.

The Houthis claimed to have fired missiles at the Saudi oil tanker NCC Ghazal, forcing it to turn back. Last week, they announced a blockade of Saudi shipping, putting another key Middle Eastern waterway — the Bab el-Mandeb strait leading to the Red Sea — at risk.

Small boats line the shore as cargo ships and other commercial vessels appear anchored in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, Monday, July 27, 2026 Razieh Poudat/AP Photo/Razieh Poudat

The United States and Iran had experienced a period of calm, during which neither side announced attacks for days following weeks of fighting over the strategic Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf waterway and narrow chokepoint through which 20% of the world’s traded oil normally flows.

The fighting flared at the end of a month packed with multiple pressure points on US President Donald Trump. In recent weeks, four US troops were killed during the fighting, while the Pentagon asked an increasingly sceptical Congress for money to cover the conflict’s ballooning costs.

World.title: Barter returns in app form: pay with your time instead of money
World.content:
Barter, the oldest form of exchange known to humankind, is enjoying an unexpected second youth. In a context marked by inflation, rising living costs and economic uncertainty, more and more people are looking for ways to access services without having to use money.

 

Paradoxically, the answer is coming in the form of technology: a new generation of apps is reviving the spirit of traditional exchange, replacing money with time, knowledge and skills. What for centuries meant swapping goods or favours between neighbours has now moved into the digital realm.

Instead of paying for a service, users exchange what they know how to do. A tax specialist can help with a tax return in exchange for Japanese cookery classes; someone with experience in artificial intelligence can receive advice on planning a trip; and a language teacher can learn photography without spending a single euro.

Time as currency

This return to bartering comes at a time when the sharing economy continues to gain ground and many households are seeking new ways to optimise their resources. In contrast to the logic of conventional consumption, these platforms encourage people to make use of an asset that almost everyone has: knowledge.

The idea is to use time as a form of currency. The SACO app has been developed by two Spanish entrepreneurs. Its operation breaks with the usual models for buying and selling services: money does not exist here. The unit of exchange is minutes. Every time a user provides a service, they accumulate time, which they can later use to request help from anyone else in the community.

The system is designed to make it easier to exchange knowledge without the need for direct financial compensation. "It is a return of barter in a modern, digital version," explains one of the co-founders, Spanish psychiatrist of Japanese descent, Kazuhiro Tajima.

The platform brings together a wide variety of profiles, from private language or music tutors to specialists in graphic design, artificial intelligence, tax advice, sport, cooking or travel. Even everyday skills that are not usually seen as a profession can become a valuable service for other users.

Talent has value

The proposal is based on a simple idea: almost everyone has some skill that could be useful to others. Yet very often that knowledge never gets monetised, either because the person who has it does not see themselves as a professional or because they had simply not found an easy way to offer it. "Everyone has some innate talent they fail to value, or that they do not monetise out of fear or embarrassment," says the app’s creator, Kazuhiro Tajima.

Rather than generating income, these platforms turn that knowledge into a currency that makes it possible to access other services without any outlay. Although bartering has never completely disappeared, its promoters believe it tends to resurface in times of economic difficulty.

"Barter is the first form of economy and it has never entirely disappeared. In times of crisis there is always a resurgence," says Tajima. Economic uncertainty, together with the search for ways to cut costs, is fuelling interest in models where access to certain services depends more on personal abilities than on purchasing power.

It is also a trend that fits with the rise of the circular and sharing economy, in which sharing resources, reusing knowledge and making use of underused skills is increasingly attractive.

The human factor

The growth of these platforms also reflects another phenomenon: the desire to preserve the human element in an era defined by artificial intelligence. Although tools such as ChatGPT or virtual assistants can resolve many queries in seconds, they cannot fully replace hands-on experience, personal context or direct, person-to-person learning.

The promoters of SACO believe that this kind of exchange not only helps save money, but also creates new social connections and highlights the value of skills that often go unnoticed. To build trust, the platform includes a rating system similar to that of other sharing-economy apps.

At a time when technology seems to be pushing aside many traditional forms of interaction, the resurgence of bartering shows that some of the oldest ideas in economics can find a new lease of life precisely thanks to digital innovation. Instead of coins, banknotes or cards, the new currency is time, experience and knowledge.

World.title: Rescuers scramble to locate survivors as death toll climbs to 13 after powerful quake hits southwestern Japan
World.content:
13 people were found dead as rescue efforts continued into Wednesday after a powerful earthquake struck part of Japan’s southwestern regions, according to a statement by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

 

“There are people who are still waiting to be rescued, and it’s a race against time,” said Takaichi. “We will go all out to find and rescue as many people as we can.”

Many people were reported missing prompting major search and rescue efforts to take place. A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the Kumamoto area on the southern main island of Kyushu late on Tuesday afternoon.

Takaichi offered her condolences to the victims and their families, and reassured the public that all necessary response units have been mobilised to save as many people as possible. The Japanese premier also urged those affected by the tremor to exercise caution as a heatwave peaking at close to 40 degrees Celsius grips the Kumamoto prefecture.

The tremor is the biggest to hit the region in a decade. In 2016, a series of earthquakes, the largest recorded at 7.0 magnitude, struck the Kumamoto area, killing 277 people and injuring close to 3,000 others.

“The shaking reminded me of the Kumamoto quake (10 years ago) and I was frightened,” said Hiroki Shimoda, an official at Mifune town hall, who saw roof tiles of nearby homes crash to the ground.

Japan's Self Defence Forces joined rescue workers in the search and rescue operations at a badly damaged shopping mall and helped deliver water and transfer the injured to nearby hospitals for medical attention.

The government is also preparing to deliver food and other critical necessities to the hard-hit areas, she said.

AEON Mall, which was destroyed by an explosion following an earthquake, is seen in Kashima, Kumamoto Prefecture, southern Japan, Wednesday, July 29, 2026 Hiro Komae/Copyright 2026 The AP. All rights reserved

The quake collapsed the second floor of the Aeon Mall in Kashima Town, trapping people underneath the rubble, according to the fire department in the prefectural capital of Kumamoto. Local officials said they are investigating an explosion reportedly from a gas leak.

The Kumamoto emergency team said a chimney collapsed at the Nippon Paper Industries Co.’s Yatsushiro factory, trapping people under the debris. As of Wednesday, seven people were feared to still be trapped, while two survivors were safely rescued. The bodies of two other people were found and removed from the same area, according to the officials.

The area is also home to several civilian-purposed nuclear plants, but authorities announced on Tuesday that the facility had not suffered major damage, and that “no abnormalities were recorded”. The affected Japanese prefecture is about 900 kilometres southwest of the capital Tokyo.

Police officers control the traffic near AEON Mall, which was destroyed by an explosion following an earthquake, in Kashima, Kumamoto, southern Japan, Wednesday, July 29, 2026 Hiro Komae/Copyright 2026 The AP. All rights reserved

Local Japanese news outlets reported that a hospital in the city of Yatsushiro took in about 40 people with injuries while about 50 others were taken to a hospital in Kumamoto city.

Many major manufacturers in Kyushu suspended operations on Tuesday but upon finding no major damage, planned to resume work from Wednesday. The runway at Aso Kumamoto Airport remains closed however, with no immediate news on when it would reopen.

A train derailed and fell on its side at Yatsushiro station, and stone walls were damaged at Kumamoto Castle, a main tourist destination that also sustained heavy damage in the 2016 quakes and is still being repaired.

Shinji Kiyomoto, director of earthquake and tsunami countermeasures with the Japan Meteorological Agency, urged residents to be cautious over the next two to three days, warning of possible strong aftershocks.

World.title: Roberto Mancini returns as Italy coach after third straight World Cup miss
World.content:
Roberto Mancini is the Azzurri's new coach – the veteran who led the Azzurri to glory at Euro 2020 has once again been tasked with revitalising a team in crisis nearly three years after he stepped down to manage Saudi Arabia.

 

Italian football federation president Giovanni Malagò announced Mancini as the new Italy coach on Tuesday, adding that Claudio Ranieri will become the new technical director after Paolo Maldini stepped down the previous day — just 16 days after being appointed.

“Time was running out … I believed the person who should become the new coach of Italy is Roberto Mancini, for a whole list of reasons,” Malagò said. “There will be a press conference tomorrow with both Claudio Ranieri and Roberto Mancini.”

The 61-year-old Mancini led the Azzurri to the European Championship title in 2021 but shockingly resigned as Italy coach in August 2023, taking over Saudi Arabia’s national team two weeks later.

“It is clear that all the necessary assessments have been made,” Malagò said when asked about Mancini's sudden departure three years ago. “I certainly took it into consideration; I am aware of his recent apologies, and obviously, everyone has made the appropriate evaluations.”

The Italian national team is in crisis after failing for a third straight time to qualify for the World Cup, prompting the resignations of FIGC president Gabriele Gravina and coach Gennaro Gattuso in April, shortly after the playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

Pirlo, Guardiola and Ancelotti dropped

The appointment comes after Andrea Pirlo was dropped as the leading candidate for the Italy job amid political concerns over a sponsorship deal with a Russian betting firm.

That led to the departures of Maldini and special adviser Leonardo by what Malagò stressed was “mutual consent".

“Practically before we had even started, we were dealing with a unique situation,” Malagò added. “There was no conflict. With utmost respect, like in the best families, there was a calm discussion and a clear and serene consensus that it was best to go our separate ways.”

Earlier, prominent figures Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti had already turned down offers to coach the Azzurri. Former Italy coach Antonio Conte was also in contention.

Mancini's first spell and record

Mancini's first stint as Italy's coach began right after the team's qualification playoff loss to Sweden prevented them from qualifying for the 2018 World Cup.

In the year-delayed Euro 2020, he revitalised the Azzurri by bringing flair and youth to a team that gained admirers across the continent and defeated England in a penalty shootout for the trophy at Wembley Stadium.

Mancini led Italy to a world record 37 games without a loss between 2018 and 2021.But in 2022, the Azzurri were eliminated from the World Cup once more due to a 1-0 home semifinal playoff loss to 67th-ranked North Macedonia.

Despite this, Mancini remained in his role until his unexpected resignation in August 2023.

Before leaving Saudi Arabia last month, he most recently worked as a coach at Al-Sadd in Qatar in 2024.

Mancini previously led Manchester City and Inter Milan to league victories in the past.

World.title: Trump and Netanyahu hold first face-to-face talks since their 'disagreement' on the Iran war
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and US President Donald Trump had an "extremely positive" meeting in Washington on Tuesday in which they committed to ensuring Iran never possessed nuclear weapons, a senior source in the premier's delegation said.

 

"It was an extremely positive meeting. The Prime Minister and President held an excellent and comprehensive discussion on the key issues of the day, first and foremost Iran," the unnamed source was quoted as saying in media reports.

"The leaders reaffirmed their ironclad commitment to ensuring that Iran never has nuclear weapons."

The talks lasted about 90 minutes and were described by the White House as "positive and productive."

The discussions were expected to focus on the war with Iran, which has paused in recent weeks as Washington pursues diplomacy.

"We will discuss all the issues on the agenda, first and foremost Iran. Naturally, our goal is to safeguard our security and also to expand the circle of peace around us," Netanyahu said before departing from Israel.

The meeting was the eighth between Trump and Netanyahu since the US president returned to office in early 2025 and came ahead of elections in Israel and US midterms later this year.

It is also their first since the latest US-Iran hostilities that flared earlier this month, after an April ceasefire collapsed. Israel did not take part in the latest fighting.

Related Zelenskyy meets Trump at White House as Ukraine seeks more US support

Shortly after arriving in Washington, Netanyahu attended a private memorial dinner on Monday evening for the late Senator Lindsey Graham and was due to attend his memorial service later on Tuesday, according to his office.

The leaders were also expected to discuss implementation of a US-backed agreement between Israel and Lebanon, as well as stalled efforts to rebuild Gaza.

Nearly three years after the war between Israel and Hamas began, the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire, and Israel continues to regularly target people the military says are 'militants'.

Relations between Trump and Netanyahu reached a low point in April during negotiations over the Iran ceasefire, with Trump publicly criticising the Israeli leader.

Trump later described Netanyahu as "a very difficult guy" in an interview, while Netanyahu dismissed the exchanges as "tactical disagreements," saying they remained aligned on the war's objectives.

World.title: US: Trump's intelligence chief pick Jay Clayton confirmed by Senate
World.content:
Clayton's appointment comes as Trump lately has renewed false claims about the 2020 election, drawing scrutiny over the administration's handling of intelligence agencies ahead of the midterms.

The US Senate on Tuesday confirmed Jay Clayton as Director of National Intelligence at a time when President Donald Trump has started reiterating his false claims about the 2020 election, which he lost.

The 51-47 vote in the Senate was along party lines with Republicans supporting the appointment and Democrats voting against.

After the vote, Trump heaped praise on Clayton posting on Truth Social: "Jay is outstanding in every way, and will do a spectacular job as Director!"

Clayton stresses he isn't 'an election denier'

Clayton will now lead the 18 intelligence agencies, including the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA), National Security Agency (NSA), and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), which have been reeling from leadership turmoil and staff cuts.

He is a former Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chairman and US attorney for the Southern District of New York.

Democrats opposed Clayton's nomination after he repeatedly declined during his confirmation hearing to explicitly state that Joe Biden won the 2020 presidential election, saying only that the result had been "certified."

"I'm not an election denier," Clayton said, without directly answering the question.

Trump renews voter fraud claims

Clayton replaces Tulsi Gabbard, who resigned in June, and Trump temporarily installed Bill Pulte as acting intelligence chief.

Pulte, a Trump loyalist with no national security experience, oversaw a tumultuous tenure marked by a roughly 30% staff reduction and the release of 2020 intelligence documents detailing China's capacity to interfere in US politics and vulnerabilities in the election system.

Trump lately has renewed false claims about the 2020 election, drawing scrutiny over the administration's handling of intelligence agencies ahead of the US midterm elections.

California Democratic Senator Adam Schiff told CNN that Clayton's refusal to unequivocally state that Biden won the 2020 election "suggests that if the president [Trump] wants the intelligence agencies to cook up something to justify voter interference in the midterm elections, that Jay Clayton doesn't have the backbone to stand up to him."

World.title: Iran war: US, Saudi Arabia strike Iran-backed Iraqi militias
World.content:
07/29/2026 July 29, 2026 US, Saudi forces hit Iran-aligned targets in Iraq

The US military says it has carried out precision strikes with Saudi forces against Iran-aligned militants in eastern Iraq.

US and Saudi fighter jets hit several weapons storage and logistics sites, US Central Command, or CENTCOM, said on X.

CENTCOM said the operation followed more than 30 drone attacks over the previous 72 hours. The US military accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of directing the strikes against US troops and Saudi energy infrastructure.

CENTCOM said the attacks on American forces failed.

Earlier, CENTCOM said it had thwarted an attempted Iranian "surprise attack" involving several ballistic missiles fired at US forces in the Middle East.

All the missiles were intercepted, the US military said. While CENTCOM did not identify their intended target, US news outlet Axios reported that they were heading towards a US military base in Jordan.

The attack came despitePresident Donald Trump's announcement that US strikes on Iran had been paused to give negotiations more time.

World.title: Japan: Rescue 'race against time' after deadly earthquake hits Kumamoto
World.content:
Dozens of people were hospitalized after the earthquake hit southern Japan. According to media reports, at least two women were killed after a shopping mall partially collapsed in the town of Kashima.

A powerful 7.1-magnitude earthquake struck Kumamoto Prefecture on Japan's southern island of Kyushu on Tuesday afternoon, triggering emergency warnings and prompting authorities to assess the extent of the damage.

On Wednesday, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said 13 people have been found dead since the earthquake struck. She added that many other people were still missing, suggesting the death toll was not final.

What do we know about the rescue efforts?

By Wednesday, over 9,000 people were in evacuation centers amid the rescue efforts.

"We have received reports of seven people with serious injuries and 29 with minor injuries. Furthermore, as of 7:00 am today (2200 GMT Tuesday), 9,186 people have sought refuge in 506 evacuation centers across five prefectures, including Kumamoto and Fukuoka," government spokesman Minoru Kihara said.

At least two of the victims died in a shopping mall in Kashima and the third died in a building collapse in a town near the epicenter.

Japan's public broadcaster, NHK, reported that "many people" were trapped inside the shopping mall damaged by the earthquake.

Several people were rescued from the mall, including a person who was reported to be in cardiopulmonary arrest.

The collapse of the mall followed an explosion likely triggered by a gas leak, NHK reported.

"Even now, there are people waiting to be rescued, and this is a race against time. We will marshal all available resources on the ground to save and rescue as many people as possible," Takaichi told reporters ‌at her office in ⁠Tokyo ⁠a day after the quake struck.

Authorities assess damage as tsunami threat eases

Prime Minister Takaichi also said initial reports indicated multiple injuries, damage to civilian infrastructure, and fires in several affected areas.

"We are still assessing the extent of injuries and property damage, but I have been informed that there have already been several injuries," Takaichi said.

"Power outages and fires are happening in some areas, and roads and bridges have been damaged and buildings collapsed," she added.

Although the earthquake caused widespread disruption and temporarily raised fears of a tsunami, officials later confirmed that the threat had subsided and that Japan's coastline was no longer in danger.

"This earthquake occurred inland, and no tsunami activity has been observed so far," a spokesperson for the Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) said. "For this reason, we hope to lift the tsunami advisory at a relatively early stage, depending on future sea level conditions."

The earthquake struck at 4:27 p.m. local time and registered the highest possible level of seven on Japan's Shindo intensity scale, which measures ground shaking Image: Kyodo/REUTERS

Power and nuclear facilities remain safe

Japan's Nuclear Regulation Authority reported that no abnormalities were detected at three nearby nuclear power plants, providing reassurance in a country still sensitive to nuclear safety concerns following the 2011 Fukushima disaster.

However, the earthquake disrupted electricity supplies across the region. According to Kyushu Electric Power, approximately 45,000 households and facilities in Kumamoto temporarily lost power following the tremor.

Several major industrial facilities are located near the earthquake zone, including operations belonging to Sony and the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC), the world's largest contract chipmaker. Sony stated that it was evaluating conditions at its facilities, while TSMC did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Japan's long history of major earthquakes

Kumamoto is no stranger to devastating seismic events.

In 2016, the region was struck by two major earthquakes, first a magnitude 6.5 quake and then a magnitude 7.3 tremor two days later. The disaster claimed 273 lives, injured more than 2,800 people. Thousands of buildings were either damaged or destroyed, making it one of Japan's most destructive recent earthquake disasters.

More recently, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck northern Japan on June 25, causing little damage and no fatalities. Earlier this year, on April 20, a magnitude 7.7 earthquake in northern Japan injured at least ten people and shook high-rise buildings as far away as Tokyo, prompting authorities to issue a temporary advisory warning of an increased risk of even stronger earthquakes. That advisory was lifted a week later.

Powerful earthquake hits southern Japan To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

One of the world's most earthquake-prone nations

Japan sits along the western edge of the Pacific "Ring of Fire," one of the most active seismic zones on Earth where four major tectonic plates meet.

Home to approximately 125 million people, the country experiences hundreds of earthquakes every year and accounts for roughly 18% of the world's seismic activity.

While most tremors are relatively minor, Japan remains haunted by memories of the catastrophic magnitude 9.0 earthquake and tsunami that struck the country's northeast coast in March 2011. The disaster killed or left missing around 18,500 people and triggered the Fukushima nuclear crisis.

Tuesday's earthquake demonstrated the country's preparedness systems, emergency response capabilities, and monitoring of critical infrastructure.

As authorities continue to assess the impact of the Kumamoto quake, residents are being urged to stay alert for potential aftershocks and follow official safety guidance.

World.title: Zelenskyy visits Trump as Ukraine seeks stronger air defense
World.content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is seeking stronger military cooperation, as Kyiv and Moscow intensify long-range strikes amid stalled peace efforts.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrived in the United States for talks with President Donald Trump on Tuesday, saying Kyiv's top priority was securing stronger air defense and strategic cooperation as Russia intensified attacks.

Trump welcomed Zelenskyy to the White House late on Tuesday morning local time, ahead of the funeral for Senator Lindsey Graham, a staunch supporter of Ukraine, who passed away earlier this month.

Images taken from behind the fences at the White House showed Zelenskyy exiting a car ready to enter the building.

White House press ‌secretary Karoline Leavitt described the meeting, which was behind closed doors, as "positive and productive."

Zelenskyy thanked Trump for the "good meeting," hailing the Republican administration's support to Kyiv in its war against Russia.

“The President and I discussed licenses for Patriot interceptor production and several other ideas that could help,” said Zelenskyy on X. “We also spoke about diplomacy — it’s important that the diplomatic process be reinvigorated.”

Later, Trump said on his Truth Social platform that the meeting "went very well!"

Zelenskyy was spotted arriving at the White House soon after his arrival in the US on Tuesday Image: Jemal Countess/UPI Photo/Newscom/picture alliance

"Our number-one priority is anti-ballistic defense and strategic cooperation with America. Peace needs to be brought closer," Zelenskyy had said in a post on X after arriving in the US.

US-Ukraine deal on Patriot production recently announced

The long-strained relations between Trump and Zelenskyy have shown modest signs of improvement in recent weeks.

Since returning to office in January last year, Trump largely stopped direct US arms shipments to Ukraine, instead leavingEuropean allies to buy American weapons and supply them to Kyiv.

However, Washington remains a key ally, providing intelligence and access to the Starlink satellite network used by Ukrainian frontline troops to communicate.

In a sign of improving ties, Trump, in a meeting with Zelenskyy in Turkey earlier this month, pledged to help Ukraine produce Patriot air defense systems, and said Kyiv would be able to produce them "pretty quickly."

This has been a long-running request from Kyiv in order to counter Russian missile attacks.

Kyiv and Moscow ramp up long-range strikes

More than four years have passed since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

Amid stalled diplomatic efforts to end the war brokered by the Trump administration, both sides have stepped up long-range strikes.

Russia said on Tuesday that more than 390 Ukrainian drones targeted the Moscow region overnight, damaging residential buildings.

Russian state media also reported that Russian forces struck two vessels, including a ship in the Black Sea that Moscow claimed was transporting military supplies for Ukraine, according to Reuters.

World.title: Guyana: Captain, crew charged with murder in ferry capsizing
World.content:
Police in Guyana have charged three men with murder in connection to a recent ferry capsizing that killed 73 and left 30 missing. Some lawmakers, however, blame government officials for the deadly accident.

Police in Guyana have formally charged three individuals with murder in connection with the capsizing of a passenger ferry that left 73 people dead and a further 30 missing on July 18.

Though the vessel had no passenger manifest, it is thought to have been carrying 179 people at the time it sank on its journey between Guyana's capital, Georgetown, and the northwestern village of Port Kaituma, near neighboring Venezuela.

Authorities say 76 passengers and crew were rescued when the vessel sank in what was the worst maritime disaster ever recorded in the South American country.

On Tuesday, the ship's captain and two crew members were formally charged at a Georgetown courthouse and remanded to prison.

The men were not required to enter pleas, had no legal representation, and will appear before the court once again on August 3.

Following the accident, Prime Minister Mark Phillips said the three men had tested positive for marijuana use.

Opposition demands resignations, commission formed to investigate accident

On Sunday, the government of Guyana set up a five-person commission of international legal and maritime experts to investigate the incident.

Opposition lawmakers have loudly called for the resignations of numerous government officials at ministries responsible for ports and for ferry services.

Although the aging MV Barima was deemed seaworthy and had a clean maintenance record, survivors reported that it was overfilled with passengers and cargo when it sank and that it had been leaking.

Though the commission is tasked with looking into those charges, the vessel itself lies on the Atlantic seabed, some 50 feet (15 meters) below the surface. Prime Minister Mark Phillips has said the vessel will not likely be salvaged.

Government officials say the MV Barima is only still in use because construction of a new Port Kaituma pier large enough to accommodate a replacement vessel recently purchased from India has not yet been completed.

World.title: UN says online scam center trafficking is skyrocketing
World.content:
Migration authorities have said gangs are trafficking ever more people to East Asian online scam centers. The UN says some 300,000 people from more than 80 countries are currently being exploited and abused.

The UN's International Organization for Migration (IOM) on Tuesday said that the number of individuals being coerced into working at massive online scam centers across Asia is increasing dramatically.

According to IOM Director General Amy Pope, an estimated 300,000 people are currently caught up in the illicit call center network, which is largely based in Cambodia, Laos and Myanmar.

Speaking in Geneva, Switzerland, on Tuesday, Pope said, "We're seeing so many more of these cases emerge right now."

"People trapped in scam compounds are victims of trafficking," said Pope, adding that unsuspecting individuals — many from Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Sri Lanka, Ethiopia and Kenya — are targeted with fake ads, often on social media, promising lucrative employment opportunities for people with strong English skills and university degrees.

Once an individual is lured in, they are often stripped of their travel documents and forced to carry out online schemes designed to defraud often older Westerners of money. Some of those trafficked are also sexually abused.

The UN estimates that some 300,000 people from more than 80 countries are kept in prison-like conditions and forced to carry out online crimes that cost unsuspecting victims billions of dollars Image: Chalinee Thirasupa/REUTERS

"The significant networks are based within Asia, but because of social media… because of the ability to ​now reach people in many, ‌many countries… their reach has expanded quite significantly," said Pope, who estimates that tens of thousands of people from over 80 countries have been trafficked.

Pope said that even when individuals manage to escape or are freed in government raids, many still face prosecution for participating in criminal endeavors.

An IOM statement published on Tuesday read: "IOM calls for continued support to assist victims of trafficking through protection, safe return and reintegration, while scaling up efforts to raise awareness of traffickers' tactics so that people can recognize risks and know where to seek help."

In Myanmar, that country's military-backed parliament approved a so-called "Anti-Online Scam Bill" on Tuesday, authorizing severe punishment and even execution for those who use, "violence, torture, unlawful arrest and detention, or cruel treatment against another person for the purpose of forcing them to commit online scams."

Myanmar's civil war, which has killed more than 100,000 people and sown instability across the country, has made it easy for scammers to set up shop inside fortified compounds, say monitors.

Chinese syndicates "constitute the major organizational force" behind the region's scam economy, running industrial-scale scam compounds in border areas and special economic zones in Myanmar, Cambodia and Laos, according to a recent UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) report.

On Tuesday, IOM cited UNODC figures that put 2025 scam center induced losses across East Asia, Australia, and New Zealand at $114 billion (€100 billion).
