World.title: Polish president obstructs windfall tax on fuel firms’ excess profits, prompting government criticism
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has condemned opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki’s “shocking decision” not to sign into law the government’s planned windfall tax on excess profits by fuel companies amid a sharp surge in fuel prices caused by the war in Iran. While Nawrocki did not veto the bill, he exercised his right to refuse to sign it and instead send it to the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) for assessment, a process that can take years. The president argued that the retroactive nature of the tax “raises serious constitutional concerns”. Nowy podatek nie obniża cen paliwa. Ma przede wszystkim dostarczyć pieniędzy do budżetu. Nie mogę zaakceptować sytuacji, w której próbę łatania finansów państwa przedstawia się obywatelom jako ochronę ich interesów, podczas gdy skutkiem będzie kolejna fala podwyżek – Prezydent… pic.twitter.com/LqI7Cojdrr — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) July 24, 2026 In mid-June, the government approved a 60% tax on excess profits from liquid fuel sales, calculated as the amount that would have been generated using a company’s average 2025 fuel sales margin, increased by 20%. The measure was expected to raise around 4 billion zloty (€927 million). When announcing the plans, the finance ministry said the levy was justified by this year’s “exceptional economic and geopolitical conditions that have led to above-average financial results in a specific segment of the fuel sector, not resulting from improved operational efficiency…but from a supply shock”. The tax was intended to offset the roughly 4.7 billion zloty the government spent on keeping fuel prices lower for consumers amid the crisis in the Middle East by, among others, cutting VAT and introducing a maximum daily price. The bill was approved by parliament on 3 July. It received support from Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, but was opposed by the right-wing and far-right opposition. According to a regulatory impact assessment, state energy giant Orlen is expected to account for about 60% of the tax base for the windfall tax, with the remaining 40% generated by other market participants. Poland’s government has approved a windfall tax on fuel companies' excess profits after the surge in energy prices due to the war in Iran. It expects the measure, which still requires parliamentary and presidential approval, to raise 4bn zloty (€940m) https://t.co/DpXa8VJDjf — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 17, 2026 The legislation then passed to Nawrocki, who has vetoed a record number of bills since becoming president last year. However, this time he instead exercised his right to refer the bill to the TK without either signing or vetoing it. In a speech announcing his decision on Friday, Nawrocki said that the proposed measures “raise serious constitutional concerns”. In particular, he criticised the fact that tax would be retroactive: it would go into force in August but would apply to revenue earned from the beginning of March. “In a democratic state governed by the rule of law, citizens and businesses must know what regulations apply at the time decisions are made,” said Nawrocki. “The state cannot change the rules a few months later and send a bill for actions taken in accordance with applicable law.” The president also argued that, ultimately, the costs of the tax would be passed on to consumers, who have already been paying much higher fuel costs since the government’s protective measures expired at the end of June. “Unfortunately, it appears that the government first lowered fuel prices for propaganda purposes, and now has decided to impose a hefty bill on Poles,” declared Nawrocki. Once a bill is sent to the TK for assessment, there is generally no time limit on how long the tribunal can take to consider it. In practice, this means that some cases can can remain unresolved for years. If the TK does find a bill to be constitutional, the president must sign it into law. Currently, a majority of judges on the TK, including its chief justice, were appointed by and are regarded as aligned with the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party that ruled Poland until 2023 and which supported Nawrocki’s presidential candidacy last year. The chief justice of the constitutional court has refused to accept four new judges appointed by parliament but whom the opposition-aligned president has refused to swear in. The decision deepens an unprecedented standoff over Poland's top court https://t.co/B02DKA3uBL — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 9, 2026 Nawrocki’s decision not to approve the windfall tax was condemned by government figures, including finance minister Andrzej Domański, who accused the president of “once again striking against Poland’s public finances”. In December, Nawrocki vetoed an increased tax on alcoholic and sweet drinks. “Instead of standing on the side of Poles, he sided with fuel corporations reaping huge profits from the current situation on the fuel market,” wrote Domański on social media. Tusk, meanwhile, wrote that the president had “blocked a bill that would have allowed taxing the gigantic profits of fuel conglomerates, making it possible to fund cheaper fuel at our stations”. He told consumers to “remember this [when you are] at the fuel pumps”. In response, the head of Nawrocki’s cabinet, Paweł Szefernaker, called Tusk an “economic dilettante” for thinking that imposing a tax would somehow lower costs rather than cause prices to rise. He instead called on the government to again lower VAT and excise duty on fuels. Od dawna wiadomo, że obecny premier jest gospodarczym dyletantem. Teraz próbuje przekonać Polaków, że nałożenie nowego podatku na paliwa sprawi, iż ceny na stacjach spadną. Zamiast nakładać kolejne podatki, proszę obniżyć VAT i akcyzę, tak jak robił to rząd Prawa i… https://t.co/3xvav6Dieu — Paweł Szefernaker 🇵🇱 (@szefernaker) July 25, 2026 The dispute over the tax comes as Poland faces an increasingly difficult fiscal situation. It had the second-largest budget deficit in the European Union last year, at 7.3% of GDP. That was far higher than the 5.5% the Polish government had pledged in 2024 when it was placed under the EU’s excessive deficit procedure. Data released last week by Eurostat showed that, in the first quarter of 2026, Poland had the EU’s third-largest annual increase in debt-to-GDP ratio, at 4.5 percentage points. In March, credit rating agency Fitch, which last year switched Poland’s credit outlook to negative, warned that the “political gridlock” between the president and the government will continue to hinder policymaking, including tackling “large fiscal deficits and rapidly rising debt”. Poland’s public debt has passed 60% of GDP for the first time, thereby exceeding the limit enshrined in EU law. The country is already under the EU's excessive deficit procedure, requiring it to take steps to bring public finances under greater control https://t.co/LNJ0YrP2Ge — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland identifies remains of legendary anti-communist resistance fighter
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s state Institute of National Remembrance (IPN) has identified the remains of Mieczysław Dziemieszkiewicz (pictured above on the right), a prominent figure in the underground resistance that fought against the Soviet-installed communist authorities in the years after World War Two. Dziemieszkiewicz, who was killed by the communist security services in 1951 and dumped in an unmarked mass grave, was identified through a combination of historical detective work and genetic testing, including exhuming the remains of his deceased mother and sister to obtain DNA samples. “Once again, we can say that the communist authorities did not win. Heroes prevail,” declared Krzysztof Szwagrzyk, deputy head of the IPN. “Even in the most difficult situations, we must seek the truth, find those of whom no trace was supposed to remain, and restore their names.” While World War Two officially came to an end in 1945, tens of thousands of Poles, known as the “cursed soldiers” (żolnierze wyklęci), continued to fight against the Soviets and the communist regime they installed in Poland. While most had laid down arms by 1947, some continued fighting well beyond then, including Dziemieszkiewicz, who operated under the nom de guerre “Rój” (meaning “swarm”). Dziemieszkiewicz, who was 20 years old when the war ended, came from a family that had been part of Poland’s wartime resistance. His anti-communist views were hardened when his elder brother, Roman, was killed by Red Army soldiers in 1945. After being conscripted that year into the Soviet-backed Polish People’s Army, Dziemieszkiewicz defected and joined the underground resistance forces, where he rose to command a unit tasked with eliminating regime officials and members of the communist Polish Workers Party (PPR). Dziemieszkiewicz’s group killed around two dozen members of the communist security services and more than 20 informants, according to the IPN. In 1950, the communist authorities intensified efforts to dismantle Dziemieszkiewicz’s unit, using threats and blackmail to recruit hundreds of agents and informants in an effort to locate the resistance fighters. Eventually, one such informant gave up Dziemieszkiewicz’s location in exchange for a promise to release her parents from captivity. Dziemieszkiewicz found himself surrounded by several hundred soldiers and was killed while trying to escape. After his body had been identified by his family, Dziemieszkiewicz was buried in a section of Powązki Cemetery in Warsaw where the remains of those killed by the communist security services were placed en masse in unmarked graves. Exhumations by the IPN, which was established after the fall of communism to investigate communist and Nazi crimes in Poland, have located over 200 complete bodies at that site as well as several thousand bone fragments. During that work, one set of remains was found buried with an eagle symbol and remnants of a black cloth. IPN researchers realised that the item was similar to a beret that appeared in posthumous photographs of Dziemieszkiewicz’s body taken by the communist security services. That prompted them to carry out genetic testing on the remains and compare them to samples taken from Dziemieszkiewicz’s mother and sister, who were buried in a cemetery in the town of Maków Mazowiecki. “We have found ‘Rój’, commander of one of the longest-fighting units of the independence underground,” declared the IPN on Friday, announcing the confirmation of his identity. They described Dziemieszkiewicz as “legend in life and a symbol of the fight against communist oppression”. The identification was announced today during a press conference at @PrzystanekH. The identification is the result of many years of work carried out by the IPN. It was preceded by extensive archival and investigative research, the analysis of forensic evidence, archaeological… https://t.co/Rcf4wemJFc pic.twitter.com/XgMUAgSQc6 — Institute of National Remembrance (@ipngovpl_eng) July 24, 2026 At a conference announcing the findings, the IPN noted that Dziemieszkiewicz’s remains had been located right next to those of another prominent anti-communist resistance fighter, Zygmunt Szendzielarz, who fought under the nom de guerre “Łupaszko”. “It is an incredible situation that two great and distinguished soldiers of the Polish underground lie next to each other in this part of the Powązki Cemetery,” said Szwagrzyk. However, Szendzielarz, who was executed by the communist authorities in 1951, has a contested legacy, given evidence that his unit was involved in the massacre of dozens of Lithuanian civilians. Some other “cursed soldiers” have faced similar accusations of war crimes. While it was often IPN historians who uncovered evidence of such actions, the institution has more recently begun to honour those figures, particularly under the rule of the national-conservative Law and Justice government between 2015 and 2023. Opposition MPs walked out of parliament yesterday as the chamber commemorated an underground officer who fought against Nazi-German occupation and the imposition of communism in Poland, but has also been accused of a war crime against civilians https://t.co/MIY7krOxTw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 9, 2022 Dziemieszkiewicz himself, however, like most of the cursed soldiers, has not faced such accusations. In 2007, President Lech Kaczyński posthumously awarded Dziemieszkiewicz the Commander’s Cross with Star of the Order of Polonia Restituta, one of Poland’s highest honours. In 2020, his image was featured on a commemorative silver coin issued by the National Bank of Poland. Through a combination of brutal repression and offering amnesties, the communist authorities managed to end most resistance efforts by 1947. However, the last “cursed soldier” to die in combat, Józef Franczak, was killed in 1963, 18 years after the end of the war. World.title: Three quarters of Poles support cooperation with Ukraine against Russia despite historical dispute
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A new study shows that, while most Poles were angered by President Volodymyr Zelensky’s recent decision to name a military unit after a group that massacred Poles in World War Two, they still overwhelmingly support cooperation with Ukraine and believe that Russia benefits from the dispute. The study, carried out by Polish state research agency CBOS, also finds that a large majority of Poles believe good relations with Ukraine will only be possible once historical issues are resolved. The polling was carried out this month in response to the ongoing diplomatic crisis that began in May, when Zelensky named a military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA)”. The UPA is widely revered in Ukraine for its role in fighting against Moscow-backed Soviet rule. However, in Poland it is associated with the Volhynia massacres, in which around 100,000 Polish civilians – mostly women and children – were slaughtered during World War Two, often with great brutality. Zelensky’s decision sparked anger in Poland, where the massacres are regarded as a genocide (though Ukraine strongly rejects that label). In June, Polish President Karol Nawrocki stripped Zelensky of the Order of the White Eagle, Poland’s highest honour, which he had received in 2023. In its new survey, CBOS found that 59% of Poles support Nawrocki’s decision, while only 28% oppose it. However, they were divided over the consequences, with 41% saying it would bring Poland more losses than benefits and the exact same proportion saying the benefits would outweigh the costs. More broadly, 84% said the Polish state should react when another country glorifies historical figures responsible for crimes against Poles. However, when asked if Ukrainians have the right to honour their own historical heroes, even if those figures left a negative mark on Polish history, 44% agreed and 42% disagreed. At the same time, over three quarters of respondents (77%) said that good Polish-Ukrainian relations could not be built without addressing the past, but a similar proportion (73%) also believe that politicians on both sides “fuel conflicts between Poles and Ukrainians for their own political gain”. The most frequently cited priorities in relations with Kyiv were security cooperation (61%), building good neighbourly relations (46%), commemorating victims of the Volhynia massacres (43%), strengthening Poland’s regional leadership (41%), and ensuring Polish companies participate in Ukraine’s reconstruction (40%). Just over half of Poles (52%) agree that “Poland and Ukraine have more common aims and interests than conflicting ones”, while 32% disagreed. A huge majority (80%) agreed that “Russia benefits from the Polish-Ukrainian dispute”. World.title: Czech Company Enters Fortune Global 500 for the First Time
World.content:
A Czech company has entered the Fortune Global 500 ranking for the first time in history.

Energy and industrial group EP Group (EPG), controlled by Czech businessman Daniel Křetínský, placed 179th in the latest edition of the prestigious list of the world’s largest companies by revenue.

The ranking, published annually by the U.S. business magazine Fortune, evaluates companies based on their total sales. EP Group reported revenues of $75.387 billion, equivalent to around CZK 1.6 trillion.

To put the figure into perspective, the Czech state budget expects total revenues of CZK 2.118 trillion this year.



EP Group’s portfolio includes stakes in major companies across Europe, including British postal operator Royal Mail, Slovak energy producer Slovenské elektrárne, German retail chain Metro and French energy giant TotalEnergies.

With its debut in the ranking, EP Group has also placed Prague among the headquarters of the world’s largest corporations. The Czech capital is now one of 242 cities worldwide where at least one Fortune Global 500 company is based.

Only 14 other countries in the Fortune Global 500 ranking have a single representative, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Poland, Austria and Thailand.

EP Group is also among a very small number of newcomers. Only 13 companies worldwide entered the top 500 this year for the first time, while another 11 returned after previously dropping out of the ranking.

The company’s rise reflects the growing importance of energy, infrastructure and industrial businesses in the global economy.

US companies dominate the ranking

American companies continue to lead the Fortune Global 500, with 141 firms making the list — the highest number since the global financial crisis in 2008.

World.title: Inside IAM Prague: How a Travelling Exhibition Laid the Foundation for One of the City’s Top-Rated Museums
World.content:
Just off Old Town Square, past the cafes and the crowds waiting for the Astronomical Clock, sits a museum that started almost by accident.

Today, IAM Prague has welcomed well over 1 million visitors from around the world and has held TripAdvisor’s Travelers’ Choice Award for five straight years.

From Shopping Malls to Old Town Square

The museum wasn’t originally supposed to be a… museum. Co-founder Jakub Bechyně and his partner Patrik Proško had been running a traveling illusion exhibit that moved between shopping malls, renting space for a month at a time before packing up and relocating. It worked, but it wasn’t permanent.

Then, in 2017, the owner of a building on Old Town Square approached them with an idea: turn part of it into a museum. The catch was the timeline. They wanted it open in two months.

Rather than build something from scratch, the team pulled from what they already had on the shelf, opening with one floor and sixteen exhibits in 2018. The collection has grown to more than 60 pieces since.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Illusion Art Museum Prague (@iamprague)

The museum moved to its current location in 2022 after the original building was sold. The new space, ideally located between Old Town Square and Wenceslas Square, needed walls removed and floors rebuilt to accommodate the art. The costs were substantial, but it turned out to be a good problem to have as the location dramatically increased the exhibition’s visibility to passersby on one of Prague’s busiest tourist thoroughfares.

Choosing Technique Over Fame

IAM Prague doesn’t chase famous names. It chases techniques. The team looks for a specific kind of illusion craft, one with real artistic quality, a genuine optical trick, and ideally a story behind it worth telling.

That approach led them to reverse-perspective specialist Patrick Hughes, and to artists whose work they discovered secondhand and eventually acquired outright rather than simply displaying on loan. In several cases, the museum ended up owning the pieces after renting them for years and deciding they belonged permanently in the collection.

About 80 percent of the exhibition has changed since opening. Early pieces built quickly to fill the space have gradually been replaced as the museum brought in stronger, more polished work from local and international artists.

The exhibition’s evolution continues, with four new pieces from international artists like Jonty Hurwitz and Andrej Boleslavsky, ranging from traditional mirror anamorphoses to digital art, recently unveiled in June.

History Hidden in Plain Sight

Much of what makes IAM Prague distinct is how it uses illusion as a delivery method for history. A glass-art piece featuring four endangered animals turns out to double as an environmental message.

A defenestration scene lets visitors reenact one of Prague’s most repeated historical events, tied to the 1618 uprising that helped trigger the Thirty Years’ War. Even the museum’s own opening date, a century after Czechoslovak independence in 1918, was picked on purpose.

One exhibit nods to Karel Čapek, the Czech writer who coined the word “robot,” a term that entered global use even though it comes from a Slavic word for forced labor.

Another traces the story of Tomáš Baťa, the industrialist who pioneered mass shoe manufacturing and built factories across multiple continents, including a Pakistani city that still carries his name today.

AI’s Impact on Art & Travel

Though much has been made on artificial intelligence’s impact on the world of art, the team’s biggest current concern isn’t AI-generated art replacing the exhibition’s themselves. It’s the shift in how travelers plan their trips.

For years, visibility depended on traditional guidebooks, online travel agencies, physical advertising, and street presence. Increasingly, travelers are relying on AI chat tools to create itineraries, shifting the importance of more “traditional” visibility mechanisms, which is forcing venues like Illusion Art Museum Prague to adapt.

Despite the changing landscape, the plan going forward leans further into digital and kinetic art, including new motion-based installations recently brought in from Berlin by artists like Florian Goerlitz.

For a museum that started as a temporary mall exhibit, the goal has stayed consistent since day one: make people stop, look twice, and leave with a story they didn’t expect to learn.

World.title: Nearly One in Five Prague Farmers’ Market Vendors Fail Veterinary Inspections
World.content:
Nearly one in five vendors inspected at Prague’s farmers’ markets during the first half of 2026 were found to have breached food safety or labeling regulations, according to the State Veterinary Administration (SVS).

Between January and June, veterinary inspectors checked 53 vendors across Prague and identified violations in 10 cases, representing almost 19 percent of all inspections.

Nationwide, inspectors carried out 165 inspections, with irregularities detected in 27 cases, or roughly 16 percent.

Officials said the most common problems in Prague involved improper storage temperatures for food of animal origin, incorrect or incomplete product labeling, and inadequate protection of food from contamination during sale.

Inspectors also highlighted several cases they considered particularly serious. In one instance, a vendor was found producing meat products without the legally required authorization while packaging them with the identification mark of a production facility that no longer exists. Authorities said such practices can mislead consumers about where products originate.



The SVS warned that food safety risks increase during the summer months, especially at outdoor markets where high temperatures make it more difficult to maintain proper cooling conditions.

Across the Czech Republic, labeling violations were the most frequently recorded offense this year, accounting for 26 cases. Problems related to hygiene and production practices—including incorrect storage temperatures and insufficient protection against contamination—followed with 22 cases.

Inspectors also documented 18 violations involving improper handling of food products and 12 cases where the origin of goods was unclear or could not be verified.

The SVS noted that a single inspection may uncover multiple breaches. While inspectors found violations in 27 inspections nationwide, the total number of individual offenses reached 82.

Inspection results remained largely unchanged compared with the same period last year. During the first six months of 2025, inspectors also carried out 165 inspections, finding violations in 16 percent of them. The main difference was that hygiene-related shortcomings topped the list last year, while labeling issues have become the most common problem in 2026.

Looking at the full year, the SVS carried out 380 market inspections across the Czech Republic in 2025, compared with 372 inspections in 2024. The proportion of inspections uncovering violations rose slightly from 17 percent to 18 percent.

World.title: Not an Official Visit: Petr Pavel Attends Hungarian GP as F1 Photographer
World.content:
The president of the Czech Republic, Petr Pavel, has made his way to the Formula 1 Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday – but was not an official visit.

Ever wondered what world leaders do in their free time? For Czech Republic president Petr Pavel, the answer is sports photography – and he’s particularly passionate about motorsport.

This weekend, he was attending the Hungarian GP with a full photography kit – and an official FIA accreditation. He arrived at the Hungaroring for Saturday’s sessions and was already taking pictures, accompanied by Czech F1 photographer Jiri Krenek.



This wasn’t the first time he was seen at a major motorsport event as a hobby photographer. Most recently, Pavel travelled to France in June to attend the Le Mans 24 Hours, once again equipped with full camera gear.

In fact, the former NATO Military Chairman has attended several races on both two and four wheels over the years.

Within the Czech Republic, Pavel covered the MotoGP and World Superbike events at Brno, while he has travelled as far as the US and Saudi Arabia to photograph NASCAR and the Dakar Rally respectively.

Last year, he also raised nearly 30,000 euros for a charity dedicated to children, single parents and the elderly by auctioning a photo album.

While it is unusual for politicians to attend races purely for leisure, several leaders regularly appear at major motorsport events in their own countries.

Last year, then British Prime Minister Keir Starmer hosted F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali, drivers and senior team figures at a reception in 10 Downing Street ahead of the British GP.

World.title: Best Petting Zoos in Prague for Families with Kids (2026 Guide)
World.content:
Prague Zoo gets all the attention — and fair enough, it’s consistently ranked among the top zoos in the world — but the city is also full of smaller, low-key spots where kids can get hands-on with animals.

These mini farms and forest parks are perfect for a relaxed weekend outing, most are free or nearly free, and several are just a short metro ride from the centre.

Here’s our pick of the best small zoos and petting farms around Prague.

1. Milíčovský dvůr – Prague 11

Right on the edge of Milíčov forest, this outdoor farm is home to a horse, an ostrich, a fox, goats, sheep, pigs, rabbits and more. Feed dispensers let kids feed the animals directly, and there’s a sandpit, a wooden playground and a small snack stand on site. Entry costs just 20 CZK. Closed Mondays.

📍 K Milíčovu 100/8, Prague 11 — nearest metro: Háje



2. Chuchle Grove Mini Zoo – Prague 5

Set on a hillside inside the Chuchle Grove nature park, this zoo run by Prague’s city forestry service cares for injured and orphaned wildlife. Expect to see mouflons, deer, wild boar, owls, lynxes and more — though petting isn’t allowed here, since the focus is conservation and education. Free entry, open 24/7, with a playground and refreshment kiosk nearby

📍 V Lázních 8, Prague 5

3. Station of Young Biologists – Prague 5

A mix of indoor and outdoor spaces near Anděl, with a tropical terrarium (crocodiles, monkeys, boas), an aviary, and outdoor pens with kangaroos, llamas, ponies and goats. Regular workshops and interactive shows run alongside the animal exhibits. General entry is free; the terrarium and greenhouses cost a small fee (20–40 CZK).

📍 Drtinova 1A, Prague 5 — near Anděl metro

4. Toulcův dvůr – Prague 10

An 8.5-hectare environmental education centre in Hostivař with cows, horses, chickens, pigs, sheep and goats, plus a cherry orchard, wetlands and a farm-to-table restaurant. Petting and feeding aren’t permitted, but it’s a beautifully kept site for a nature walk.

📍 Kubátova 1/32, Prague 10

Honourable mentions

If you’re just after a nice walk with a chance of spotting animals, these free spots are worth a detour:

Wild Garden Hostivař (Prague 15) — rare white fallow deer and mouflons roam near a flooded quarry, with a playground and lakeside walk.

(Prague 15) — rare white fallow deer and mouflons roam near a flooded quarry, with a playground and lakeside walk. Kunratice Forest (Prague 4) — sheep, dwarf goats and pigs can be fed at the “Na tý louce zelený” restaurant, with spotted deer and mouflons visible along the trails.

(Prague 4) — sheep, dwarf goats and pigs can be fed at the “Na tý louce zelený” restaurant, with spotted deer and mouflons visible along the trails. Kamýk Forest (Prague 12) — a small goat enclosure and pheasant aviary tucked next to the gamekeeper’s lodge, surrounded by walking and cycling trails.

World.title: Stromovka: A Green Paradise in the Heart of Prague
World.content:
Stromovka is one of the largest and most popular parks in Prague, drawing visitors with its beautiful nature, rich history, and numerous activities.

Let’s explore what Stromovka offers and how to get there.

Why Visit Stromovka?

Looking for a break from the city’s hustle and bustle or the perfect spot for a picnic with friends? Stromovka is your ideal choice. This vast park features green meadows, shady alleys, and ample opportunities for sports and cultural events.

What is Stromovka?

Stromovka, officially known as Královská obora, spans more than 95 hectares, making it one of Prague’s largest green spaces. Located in Prague 7, the park is a favorite among joggers, cyclists, families, and anyone looking to escape into nature without leaving the city.

It’s perfect for walks, picnics, sports, or simply relaxing on the grass.



A Brief History

Stromovka’s history dates back to the 13th century when it was established as a royal hunting ground. Over time, it evolved and expanded, becoming a public park in the 19th century. The park is home to the original Vltava Creek and several ponds, which host various water birds.

Throughout its history, Stromovka has undergone many changes, shaping it into the popular relaxation spot it is today.

Activities in Stromovka

Stromovka offers a wide range of activities for all ages. Here are some ideas:

Walking and Running: Enjoy the scenic trails.

Cycling: Explore the park on two wheels.

Picnics: Large meadows and shady spots are perfect for a picnic.

Sports: Play football, volleyball, and other sports.

Cultural Events: Attend various events hosted in the park.

How to Get to Stromovka

By Metro: The nearest metro station is Nádraží Holešovice (line C). From there, it’s just a few minutes’ walk to Stromovka.

By Tram: Trams also reach the park. The nearest stops are Výstaviště Holešovice (lines 6, 12, 17) and Planetarium Prague (line 6).

By Bike: Cycling enthusiasts can easily access Stromovka by bike. Bike-sharing stations like Rekola and Nextbike are available around the park, allowing you to ride directly into this natural haven.

World.title: August 12-31: Prague to Host Festival of New Circus Letní Letná
World.content:
The international festival of new circus and theatre, Letní Letná 2026, will take place in Prague on August 12-31.

The festival will feature over 200 performances, workshops, concerts, and various acts by circus artists from 14 countries, including a special program for children.

This year marks the 23rd edition of the festival. Letenské sady park will once again be the main venue, with tents set up to create a mini-town complete with a coffee shop and an evening bar.



Many performances will be free of charge. Additionally, the festival will offer a rich and varied daily program: children’s shows, circus, juggling and acrobat workshops, music concerts, exhibitions, lectures, creative workshops, and more.

One of this year’s highlights is Wolf by Australia’s renowned Circa ensemble. The international lineup also includes Switzerland’s Accademia Teatro Dimitri, presenting its graduate production La Grinta, and Seismic, a collaboration between French choreographer Marie Gourdain and German artist Felix Baumann, featuring Czech performers.

The Czech program includes the premiere of Vertige by AirGym Art Company, Enola by Eliška Brtnická, new productions from Losers Cirque Company, and Hey, Earth! by Cirque La Putyka.

Emerging talent will also take center stage, with performances by CZirkidz Dance Company, Teens Cirkabaret, and recent graduates of international circus schools.

Audiences will have the chance to experience works in progress, including K voknu by Michaela Stará and Filip Zahradnický, followed by discussions with the artists.

For adults, Světla a stíny by Silk&Steel explores the darker sides of human experience through aerial and ground acrobatics, while family-friendly performances include the popular (Not Only) Juggling Galashow and Orbiting Zero by Czech juggler Aleš Hrdlička.

Beyond the performances, visitors can enjoy free workshops, children’s activities, concerts, open-air events, food stalls, bars, and relaxation areas throughout the festival grounds. Babysitting is available during selected performances, and the venue is fully accessible, making Letní Letná a festival for all ages.

World.title: New Railway Tunnel to Cut Prague to Pilsen Journey to 45 Minutes
World.content:
The Czech government has approved the next phase of one of its largest railway infrastructure projects: a new tunnel connecting Prague and Beroun.

Construction is expected to begin in 2032, with completion scheduled for 2044.

The 24.7-kilometre double-track tunnel will significantly shorten travel times on one of the country’s busiest rail corridors.

Once completed, trains will travel between Prague-Smíchov station and Beroun in around 13 minutes, reducing the current journey time by more than 30 minutes.

The project will also improve connections towards western Czechia and neighbouring Germany. The journey from Prague to Pilsen is expected to take approximately 45 minutes, while international rail services to Munich and Nuremberg will become faster and more reliable.



New railway line designed for speeds of up to 200 km/h

The planned railway route will include a new high-speed section designed for trains travelling at up to 200 km/h. The tunnel will begin near Prague-Smíchov station, pass beneath the Barrandov area, and emerge near Beroun.

A separate connection on the Prague side is also planned, linking the new line with Braník Bridge and Prague-Krč. The additional infrastructure will improve connections within the capital while increasing capacity on the wider railway network.

Construction preparation underway

Preparatory work for the tunnel is already in progress. Geological surveys and technical documentation are currently being completed, with the application for a construction permit expected to be submitted between 2028 and 2029.

After the approval process, Správa železnic will launch a tender to select the construction company responsible for building the tunnel.

The Czech Railway Administration estimates the total cost of the project will continue to rise due to inflation and increasing construction expenses. However, its director general Tomáš Tóth said the estimated cost of around CZK 3 billion per kilometre remains comparable with similar railway tunnel projects abroad.

The project is expected to increase railway capacity towards western Czechia, improve timetable reliability, and strengthen connections between Prague, Pilsen, and major German cities.

World.title: Israeli man stabbed at Hungarian festival
World.content:
An Israeli man has been stabbed at the Ozora Festival, in central-western Hungary, and transported to hospital by paramedics, the Fejér County police department said on Facebook.

A member of the transformational and arts festival’s security staff alerted police early on Tuesday after an Israeli man in his 30s was stabbed on the festival grounds, the report said. Two men were taken into custody on suspicion of aggravated assault in connection with the incident, it added.

“To ensure the safety of festivalgoers, police will continue to conduct enhanced checks and are working closely with the organisers to implement the necessary security measures,” the police said.

On Monday, a Belgian, an Israeli, and a Portuguese man were apprehended on the festival grounds after being caught in the act of selling drugs. In addition to being taken into custody, proceedings were initiated against them for alleged drug trafficking.

World.title: Up to 160 new, eco-friendly low-floor trolleybuses could come to Budapest
World.content:
The Budapest Transport Centre (BKK) has paved the way for the city’s fleet to be expanded by as many as 160 new, eco-friendly, low-floor trolleybuses, should the necessary funding become available, the company said on Tuesday.

In a statement to MTI, BKK said it had signed the framework agreement for the vehicle procurement with Electrobus Europe Zrt. and Yutong, the companies that won the public tender, meaning that once the money is in place, the modernisation of Budapest’s vehicle fleet can continue, further improving the standard of public transport in the capital, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

To bring the framework agreement into force, funding for the purchase of the 40 vehicles covered by the commitment — 16 single-unit trolleybuses and 24 articulated trolleybuses — must be secured within six months of the contract being signed.

The transport organiser said it still aims to deliver the project with the help of European Union funding.

World.title: Numerous investigations surround the BYD plant in Szeged: are guest workers and Hungarian subcontractors at risk?
World.content:
The BYD plant in Szeged is one of Europe’s largest Chinese automotive investments, but the build has in recent months been shadowed not only by its rapid pace, but by fatal and serious accidents, police investigations, and apparent disregard for workplace safety and environmental rules. While construction presses ahead at full tilt, more and more questions are being raised about whether the project is being carried out under proper safety conditions, and how Chinese guest workers and Hungarian subcontractors are being treated on site.

Police investigation into 29 cases around the BYD plant

According to Magyar Hang, the Criminal Department of the Csongrád-Csanád County Police Headquarters is investigating a total of 29 cases connected to the BYD plant in Szeged. The proceedings were launched on suspicion of a range of offences, and in several instances relate to working conditions and events during the construction work.

Two fatal accidents in a few months

The greatest concern has centred on the fatal workplace accidents. Two workers died at the construction site within a matter of months. The first fatal incident occurred during loading and crane operations. Later, another Chinese worker was killed after being hit by a lorry on the construction site.

Former PM Viktor Orbán and BYD head Wang Chuanfu in Budapest. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Viktor

Professional bodies have also spoken out about the two tragedies. In their view, while construction is inherently a hazardous industry, two fatal workplace accidents in such a short period are highly unusual even on a project of this scale.

Safety concerns

Beyond the fatalities, there have been further accidents on the site. In one incident, several people were injured in a vehicle crash; on another occasion, a worker suffered serious injuries.

The Mayor of Szeged, László Botka, at the construction site. Photo: FB/László Botka

In light of the safety risks, professional organisations are calling for stricter occupational safety inspections. They say it is particularly important to establish whether all health and safety regulations are being observed during construction, and whether supervision of the work areas is adequate.

Concerns deepen

The Orbán government had previously promised BYD management that it would bring in 10,000 guest workers for the project. According to Magyar Hang, however, BYD’s leadership is treating Chinese guest workers very badly. The New York-based China Labor Watch says it found conditions in Szeged that suggest forced labour.

Some guest workers were said to have worked all seven days of the week without a day off, on shifts lasting 9-12 hours a day. In the process, they reportedly exceeded the annual overtime limit, but nobody seemed to care. Part of their wages was also withheld. Many did not even have permission to work in Hungary. It is hardly surprising, then, that inspectors were seen on the site again last week.

The authorities have also launched an investigation into breaches of environmental regulations. They found, for example, that humus-rich topsoil may have been removed from the site without the mandatory measurements and notification, and then spread over 20 hectares. On 10 per cent of that area, soil contaminated with alkylbenzenes was then laid, meaning the affected farmer must destroy the wheat grown there. Even so, BYD was fined only 10 million forints.

Magyar Hang has also previously reported that Hungarian subcontractors were not paid by BYD and left the site as a result.

Orbán government promised Chinese BYD vast subsidies and influx of thousands of guest workers

Szijjártó is now working for BYD

Last week, Péter Szijjártó, the former minister of foreign affairs and trade, announced that he would continue his career as BYD’s new global head of external relations. Szijjártó played a major role in helping the investment choose Hungary in the first place, and it also received significant government support. Since BYD moved its European corporate and development headquarters to Budapest a few months ago, Szijjártó will not have far to travel for work.

Magyar Hang notes, however, that in Western Europe this kind of post-government move is strictly restricted. “If a former state leader leaves politics and immediately goes to work for a company that places a premium on state connections — indeed, the Szeged BYD plant received billions in state support precisely during Szijjártó’s ministership — that represents a serious corruption risk and, at the same time, a conflict-of-interest problem”, it added.

Chinese BYD buys huge office building for new European HQ in Budapest’s central district

World.title: Hungary’s new key agency can begin work: are Fidesz-linked business circles and public figures targeted? – updated
World.content:
Parliament on Tuesday approved the bill establishing the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH), with MPs voting 143 in favour and 47 against. The agency’s task will be to protect public assets, uncover the unlawful management of public assets, and recover them.

The law’s explanatory memorandum says its aim is to create a legal framework that will enable the NVVH to carry out effectively the tasks needed to protect public assets, uncover the unlawful management of public assets, and recover them, the Hungarian news agency wrote.

The NVVH will be able to carry out public asset-protection risk assessments and inspections, and to order organisations to be placed under public asset-protection supervision.

Members of the Tisza parliamentary group happy with the decision. Photo: MTI

It will also have the right, in the course of its work, to enter premises, archives, warehouses, and server rooms linked to an investigation; inspect any relevant document, record, contract, or electronic data storage device; examine the payment accounts and financial assets of an organisation placed under supervision; exercise investigative and prosecutorial powers to recover and protect public assets; and request the assistance of the police, the prosecution service, the National Tax and Customs Administration, or other bodies.

The president and vice-presidents of the office will be elected by Parliament within 30 days of the law entering into force.

Update – Magyar: Europe’s most powerful anti-graft body taking shape

Europe’s strongest anti-graft institution is taking shape, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Tuesday, referring to the newly established National Asset Recovery and Protection Office (NVVH). In a video posted on social media, he stressed that the office will operate entirely independently of the government.

Parliament approved the law establishing the office on Tuesday with 143 votes in favour and 47 against.

Magyar hailed the vote as historic, calling it a major step forward for one of [ruling] Tisza’s most important initiatives.

“Despite falling-apart [opposition] Fidesz’s parliamentary group voting against the fight for transparency and the recovery of national assets, Tisza’s MPs secured the majority needed for this proposal,” he said. “Now is the time for a real reckoning to begin, for meaningful work to start, and for Europe’s most powerful anti-corruption body to finally take shape. We will provide all the necessary support to make this happen.”

The prime minister acknowledged that the public is eagerly awaiting the office’s swift and effective launch. “Hungarians rightfully expect this new anti-corruption body to handle every case with the utmost thoroughness and precision,” he added.

“Today’s law sets out our next steps,” Magyar explained. “The president and four deputy presidents of the National Asset Recovery and Protection Office must be appointed within 30 days. These positions must be filled by non-partisan, highly qualified professionals who will act in the spirit and letter of the law, serving the interests of the Hungarian people and the nation.”

Once the leadership takes office, the real work begins: recruiting investigators, financial analysts, tax experts, prosecutors, and legal specialists. “Their mission will be to uncover who stole billions of forints from the Hungarian people and how they did it,” he said.

Magyar emphasised that the NVVH will operate completely independently of the government, with the authority to initiate investigations, conduct inquiries, launch proceedings, and even prosecute cases, all strictly within the rule of law.

He condemned Fidesz for comparing the constitutionally established anti-corruption office to the AVH, the infamous secret police of Hungary’s communist era. “The AVH was a political tool of the Communist Party that tormented thousands of Hungarians,” Magyar said. “By making this vile comparison, Fidesz has dishonoured their memory.”

The prime minister reiterated that the new office was created based on the will of Hungarian voters, in full compliance with the Fundamental Law and all relevant regulations. “The goal of this new office is not political retribution or settling scores,” he said. “It is about recovering embezzled public funds and exposing serious corruption cases. But its mission goes beyond just reclaiming stolen assets or correcting past wrongs — it’s also about building a cleaner future.”

“The NVVH will play a key role in this work,” Magyar concluded. “But creating a transparent, corruption-free public life in Hungary is not the responsibility of this super-agency alone. It is up to all of us, every single day.”

World.title: Hungarian passport remains one of the world’s strongest — but why, and can it climb higher?
World.content:
The Hungarian passport is ranked alongside those of Croatia, Poland, South Korea and Malta as one of the world’s most powerful travel documents. But how does a country rise ever higher up the rankings — and what explains Hungary’s success?

Hungary’s passport remains highly prized

Many people assume a passport’s value is determined primarily by the country that issued it. In reality, what matters far more is how many countries its holder can enter easily, without the lengthy business of securing a visa in advance. On that measure, Hungary performs exceptionally well: according to the latest international rankings, the Hungarian passport is among the world’s four strongest.

Indeed, the latest Passport Index places the Hungarian passport in a respectable fifth position among the world’s most powerful travel documents. It is worth noting, however, that several countries can share the same ranking, which is why Hungary occupies this spot alongside Croatia, Latvia, Poland, Malta and South Korea.

The United Arab Emirates remains comfortably at the top, having held first place for some time. Emirati citizens can travel visa-free to 138 countries, must obtain a visa on arrival at a further 44, and need to apply in advance for just 16.

Singapore is in second place. Its citizens can also travel to 138 countries, though only 37 require a visa on arrival.

Spain and Malaysia share third place, while Belgium, Luxembourg, France, Japan, Denmark, Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands, Italy, Finland, Switzerland, Greece, Portugal, Austria, Norway and Ireland are tied in fourth.

Then comes the “Hungarian group” mentioned above. In the region, only the Austrian passport ranks higher than Hungary’s. It is also striking that the Hungarian passport outranks those of Great Britain, Canada, the United States and even the Vatican.

The Hungarian passport that enables you to travel freely in the Schengen Zone. Photo: Daily News Hungary

Hungarian citizens can travel visa-free to 129 countries, need to obtain a visa on arrival in 43, and must secure one before departure for 26 destinations.

At the bottom of the table are countries such as Afghanistan, Iraq and Syria, as well as Pakistan.

Refused or terminated? What one missed appointment taught an American about Hungarian residency

What makes a passport “strong”?

Passport strength is calculated using so-called mobility points. This measures how many destinations a country’s citizens can enter in simplified form — in other words, without having to submit a lengthy visa application in advance to an embassy or consulate.

Four types of entry are counted towards the total:

visa-free entry;

visa on arrival;

electronic travel authorisation (ETA);

fast-track, online e-visa.

The more countries a passport holder can reach through one of these routes, the higher that passport rises in the international rankings, according to Index.

Hungary benefits greatly from Schengen membership, as the zone continues to abolish visa requirements for other countries which, on a reciprocal basis, take similar measures. It is precisely for this reason that the United States has slipped to ninth place, following tightening introduced under the Trump administration.

World.title: Historic drought: Paks NPP output cut, Romanian NPP reactor offline due to River Danube’s low water level
World.content:
The government has made preparations if any steps are needed to ensure Hungary’s secure energy supply, Economy and Energy Minister István Kapitány said in a post on Facebook on Tuesday. Kapitány acknowledged a cut in the output of the Paks nuclear power plant. Furthermore, Romania has taken one of the reactors at its Cernavodă nuclear power station offline because of the exceptionally low water levels in the Danube

Kapitány acknowledged a cut in the output of the Paks nuclear power plant due to record-low water levels on the Danube, which the NPP uses for cooling, and warned that another heatwave could arrive in Europe in the coming days, boosting demand for electricity even as water levels fall further.

“We have prepared for this situation,” he said, adding that the ministry is in constant contact with the Paks NPP, transmission system operator MAVIR and state-owned energy company MVM.

“We have held professional-level consultations and are assessing developments from hour to hour,” he said. “We are managing the situation in a responsible and transparent manner, in compliance with all professional norms,” he added. Kapitány said the public would be updated on any important developments.

The Paks NPP said it cut output of its number 1 block by 254 MW in the evening on Monday as water levels on the Danube reached -106cm.

Danube reaches record low in Budapest

An all-time record low water level in the River Danube of 31 centimetres was registered in central Budapest on Tuesday morning, breaking an earlier record of 33 centimetres, the water management directorate (OVF) reported. The authority noted that all Europe’s rivers are critically low.

Another heat dome approaches Hungary while the Danube reaches historic low water levels. Photo: Facebook/Valyo, város és a folyó

Romania shuts down nuclear reactor as Danube runs low

Romania has taken one of the reactors at its Cernavodă nuclear power station offline because of the exceptionally low water levels in the Danube, the plant’s operator said on Tuesday.

State-owned Nuclearelectrica said the No 1 reactor had been disconnected from the national grid and shut down because of severe drought and the river’s reduced flow. The Danube provides cooling water for the plant, and its discharge has fallen to an unprecedented level in the past three decades. The lowest reading, 1,750 cubic metres a second, was recorded on 16 July.

The end draws near for Lake Velence as Danube hits a record low in Budapest: will Hungary dry out this year?

Nuclearelectrica said it was in постоян contact with the authorities responsible for water management and would not rule out shutting down the second reactor, depending on how river levels develop. At present, the No 1 unit is not expected to restart before 4 August at the earliest.

Romania’s only nuclear power station first went into operation in 1996. The plant, near Cernavodă on the Danube close to the Black Sea, has two reactors built using Canadian Candu technology and together they generate about 20 percent of the country’s electricity.

World.title: Video: Ferocious storm slams Hungary, ripping up trees as if they were tomato stakes
World.content:
A rarely seen, gale-force windstorm has torn through north-eastern Hungary, Transcarpathia, and the north-western and eastern regions of Romania and Slovakia. The cold front that passed quietly and almost dry across much of Hungary yesterday wreaked considerable damage in these areas. Here are some of the images and footage.

Ferocious storm slams Hungary

Fülesd is a small village of fewer than 400 inhabitants in Szabolcs-Szatmár-Bereg county, close to both the Hungarian–Romanian and Hungarian–Ukrainian borders. It was here that yesterday’s devastating, tornado-like windstorm struck, sweeping away large trees as if they were mere tomato stakes. In nearby Kispalád, a hailstorm of a kind not seen for many years battered the village, with walnut-sized hailstones falling everywhere.

As we also reported, yesterday a moderate cold front reached Hungary and raced across the Carpathian Basin, but it did not bring significant rainfall. In north-eastern Hungary and eastern Slovakia, however, it developed into a chain of thunderstorms that ripped through these regions, bringing hail, tornado-like winds and relatively large amounts of sudden torrential rain. In Fülesd, a recently published video suggests that a short-lived whirlwind may also have formed.

Hail fell in Mikota and Tiszakóród. According to idokep.hu, these chunks of ice were lifted up and down repeatedly within the thundercloud for a long period.

One eyewitness said he had never seen anything so frightening, as the gale-force winds toppled trees one after another and tore roofs from residential buildings. You can watch the terrifying footage below:

In the area around Csenger, Csengerújfalu and Tyukod a striking funnel cloud formed, although this is not connected with the possible tornado in Fülesd, as that occurred later. Here are some of the pictures:

Over Uzhhorod, the storm arrived with brutal hail:

Transcarpathia power supply cut

Across the region, the storm caused severe damage. According to MTI, in Transcarpathia power supply has been completely cut in 38 settlements and partially disrupted in a further 64, as a result of Monday’s late-afternoon storm, which in places was accompanied by hailstones the size of walnuts.

Another brutal heat dome arrives as Danube nears record low — what to expect this week

According to the Kárpáti Igaz Szó news portal, in the district centred on Berehove, which is largely populated by ethnic Hungarians, the worst damage was suffered by Bene, Makkosjánosi and Sárosoroszi, where the roofs of family homes, several schools and kindergartens were damaged.

Meteorology: capital’s wind record broken on Monday

The capital’s wind record was broken on Monday, HungaroMet Zrt. reported on its website on Tuesday. It said that on János Hill in Budapest, instruments measured winds of 85 kilometres per hour in the early afternoon’s storm, beating the previous daily record for the strongest gust in the capital. The earlier record for this date was 83 kilometres per hour, also measured on János Hill, in 2019.

World.title: Video: Century-old Ford Model T takes centre stage at Hungarian National Museum
World.content:
A 100-year-old Ford Model T has arrived at the Hungarian National Museum, where it was carefully lifted by crane and wheeled into the building under strict conservation measures on Monday morning. The historic vehicle will feature in the museum’s upcoming exhibition, The American Dream, opening to the public on Thursday, the museum noted.

Ford Model T in the Hungarian National Museum

The Ford Model T, a centrepiece of the Transport Museum’s collection, holds special significance as its design involved two Hungarian engineers, József Galamb and Jenő Farkas. Curators Klára Radnóti and Angelika Orgona chose to include it in the exhibition to highlight this connection. The car, exactly a century old this year, boasts a 3,500cc engine with 18 horsepower and remains fully operational.

The American Dream exhibition, marking the 250th anniversary of US independence, will showcase not only the Ford Model T but also a wealth of fascinating artefacts. At its heart, the exhibition explores the lives of Hungarians who emigrated to America, alongside the stories of famous figures who spent time in the US, including Lajos Kossuth, Albert Szent-Györgyi, Zsazsa Gábor, and Zita Szeleczky, with personal mementoes on display.

The American Dream – Hungarians in the United States, 1776–2026 will run from 30 July to 1 November.

World.title: British investor Ghai Sant Ram acquires plot near Bucharest for new residential project
World.content:
British investor Ghai Sant Ram announced the purchase of a plot of approximately 30,000 square meters from fiery Romanian businessman and football club owner George Becali on Tuesday, July 28.

The purchase price was approximately EUR 14.3 million, and the land was acquired together with the building permit for a large-scale real estate development. The transaction was brokered by CGA Home Consulting through Cătălin Apetri (right), the company’s CEO and founder, who also serves as Romania Development Director for Ghai Family Holding and Ghai Sant Ram.

The plot located near Pipera Plaza, northern Bucharest, was acquired via Ghai Family Holding. The investor intends to develop a residential project comprising approximately 650 apartments on the newly acquired land.

“The Pipera area, where the newly acquired plot is located, has genuine residential demand, driven both by northern Bucharest’s business hub and by rapid access to infrastructure, services, schools and shopping centers. The area’s long-term potential underpins our decision to invest here in a new residential development comprising 650 apartments,” said Cătălin Apetri, CEO and founder of CGA Home Consulting and Romania Development Director for Ghai Family Holding.

Ghai Sant Ram has more than two decades of experience in residential development across the United Kingdom and Romania. The British investor previously developed Ivory Residence and Horizon City in Romania.

Details of the new development’s exact configuration, apartment mix, number of parking spaces, amenities, total investment value and construction timetable will be announced once the technical stages have been completed.

The plot's “location provides easy access both to central Bucharest and to Voluntari, Tunari, DN1, the Bucharest Ring Road and the A3 motorway. Proximity to Tei Park and Herăstrău Park is another major advantage, while the location is also relevant for families working in northern Bucharest,” said Cristian Stanciu (left), CEO of the Ivory Residence and Horizon City residential projects.

With the 650 new apartments planned on the plot, Ghai Sant Ram’s residential portfolio in Romania will exceed 2,500 units overall.

World.title: PwC: Bucharest Stock Exchange capitalization exceeded EUR 100 bln for first time in history in 2025
World.content:
The market capitalization of the Bucharest Stock Exchange exceeded the EUR 100 billion threshold (RON 537.7 billion) for the first time in its history at the end of 2025, the highest level in the past 19 years, and growth accelerated in 2026, according to the ninth edition of the PwC Romania report “Bucharest Stock Exchange and M&A valuation multiples.”

The Regulated Market accounted for RON 523.7 billion, up by 49% compared to 2024, while the MTS/AeRO segment reached RON 14.6 billion, up by 15%. The BET index increased by 46% in 2025, to 24,439 points, its best annual performance since 2009, while the BET-TR index, which also reflects the dividends paid by its constituent companies, advanced by 55%, to 57,230 points, ranking among the top-performing equity indices globally.

“2025 was a landmark year for the local capital market. Despite a backdrop marked by a large budget deficit, the highest inflation rate in the European Union and persistent geopolitical tensions, the BET index delivered its best annual performance in 16 years, and market capitalization exceeded EUR 100 billion for the first time. MSCI’s reclassification of Romania as an Advanced Frontier Market in June 2025, along with FTSE Russell’s confirmation of 14 Romanian companies in its global indices, shows that international investors’ interest in the local market is strengthening,” said Sorin Petre, Leader of the Valuation and Economics department at PwC Romania.

2025 and the first part of 2026 brought three initial public offerings that were large by the standards of the local capital market, alongside several smaller transactions. The three major deals completed were: Cris-Tim Family Holding (RON 454 million, 42x oversubscription, November 2025), Electro-Alfa International (RON 579.6 million, 60x oversubscription, March 2026) and Christian ’76 Tour (RON 149 million, June 2026).

The number of active retail investors on the BVB grew from 226,000 at the end of 2024 to over 285,000 at the end of 2025, an increase of 26% and four times the level recorded in 2020.

“Although market capitalization grew by 49% in 2025, traded value decreased slightly, by 1%, which shows that the strong appreciation in prices was not matched by a similar rise in trading activity, with liquidity remaining concentrated in a limited number of issuers,” added Sorin Petre.

The five most traded shares on the Regulated Market in 2025 were Banca Transilvania (28% of total traded value), OMV Petrom, Hidroelectrica, Aquila Part Prod Com and Romgaz, together accounting for 58% of total traded value. As in previous years, they belonged to the financial services, Oil & Gas and Electricity sectors.

The average return of the capital market, more than the risk-free rate, which rewards investors for taking on higher risk, was 7.6% for the BET index and 15.3% for the BET-TR index over the period 2015–2025.

In 2025, the excess return reached 37% for BET and 45% for BET-TR, against a risk-free rate of 6.8%. Romania’s equity market capitalisation to GDP ratio stood at 27.7% as of 31 December 2025, higher than in previous years but still below the levels observed in other regional markets such as Greece, Croatia, and Hungary.

The number of BVB-listed companies with ESG scores reached 24 at the end of 2025, with a combined market capitalisation of RON 280.8 billion. Companies in the Oil & Gas, Electricity and Financial services sectors account for approximately 90% of the capitalisation of the companies with an ESG score.

With a significantly larger number of listed companies (331) and a total capitalization of EUR 105.5 billion, companies listed on the BVB remain on average smaller than those listed on markets such as Poland, Greece or Czechia, which positions the BVB as a mid-sized market in the region.

The local bond market also reached a record level in 2025, with total issuance of EUR 6.3 billion (RON 31.8 billion), almost three times the 2022 level, mostly generated by government bonds. Corporate issuance rebounded strongly, to EUR 2 billion, the highest level in the analysed period. In 2025, 27 out of the 33 corporate bond listings were carried out exclusively on international markets.

In 2025, the median EBITDA multiple of the companies listed on the BVB main market was 9.7x, while on the AeRO Premium segment it stood at 9.0x. The average EBITDA multiple derived from the analysis of transactions completed on the local market in 2025 was 7.6x, below the historical average of 8.2x. The gap might be explained by the fact that companies listed on the BVB are generally perceived as more stable, whereas private transactions often involve companies valued based on their future growth prospects.

On the Regulated Market, the highest median P/E multiple was recorded by the Consumer and Healthcare sectors (20.6x) and by IT&C (17.8x), whereas the lowest levels were observed in the Real estate (7.6x) and financial services (7.9x) sectors. The aggregate median P/E multiple was 12.7x in 2025, above the average of the last 19 years (11.2x).

World.title: Timișoara City Celebration expands accessibility with sign language concerts, inclusive spaces
World.content:
This year's Timișoara City Celebration will expand accessibility measures for people with hearing impairments and neurodiverse visitors, with sign language interpretation at several headline concerts and dedicated viewing areas. The event will take place between July 31 and August 3.

The organizers said concerts by Beth Hart, The Script, Irina Rimes, and Alexandra Căpitănescu will be interpreted into Romanian Sign Language (LSR), continuing an initiative first introduced during Timișoara's 2023 European Capital of Culture program and maintained in subsequent editions of the festival.

Romanian Sign Language interpretation will be provided by Denis Blidariu, an interpreter who has worked at concerts, festivals, theaters, cinemas, and international conferences.

The main stage area will also include a dedicated viewing platform for neurodiverse visitors, designed to provide a more comfortable concert experience and improved visibility. A separate area will be available for people with hearing impairments.

The accessibility measures are part of a broader effort by the Timișoara Project Center, one of the event's organizers, to make public cultural events more inclusive.

The 2026 edition of Timișoara City Celebration will be held under the theme "One city. A thousand ways to experience it. Diversity.”

World.title: Four bears to be transferred from Romania's Libearty Sanctuary to wildlife park in France
World.content:
Four rescued brown bears from Romania's Libearty Sanctuary in Zărnești will be relocated to a wildlife park in France as part of an international conservation partnership, Agerpres reported. The transfer, involving four young sibling bears, was described by the sanctuary's operator as an unprecedented operation for Romania.

The Millions of Friends Association (AMP), which manages the sanctuary, said the bears, named Alexandra, Anita, Chance, and Thomas, are about two and a half years old and were rescued from the wild.

They will be transported by road to Parc Animalier de Sainte-Croix after being sedated, with the journey expected to take more than a day.

“Four bears rescued from the wild and now in our care will leave Romania together for a park in France. […] It is an unprecedented transfer for AMP Libearty and a unique event for Romania," the association said.

According to AMP, as quoted by the news agency, the relocation has been planned in detail to ensure the animals' safety throughout the journey.

The organization said that the French park shares a similar vision focused on wildlife conservation and environmental education.

Parc Animalier de Sainte-Croix spans 120 hectares and is home to around 1,500 animals from 100 European wildlife species. In addition to its conservation work, the park offers visitors the opportunity to stay overnight in cabins within the park and observe the animals from close range, according to Agerpres.

World.title: IT tops sectors in Romania with highest salaries despite layoffs
World.content:
IT remained the field with the highest salaries on the Romanian market in the first half of 2026, despite the contraction in hiring volumes and even layoffs in profile companies. Salaries in the sector averaged RON 8,000, up by 5% compared to last year, according to Salario data, the salary comparator operated by eJobs.

The second best-paid sector on the market was oil and gas, with a net average of RON 7,000, followed by research and development, at RON 6,800. All three sectors were also featured in the ranking of the best-paying fields last year.

The following industries were construction/installations (RON 6,500) and engineering, telecommunications, audit/consultancy, and naval/aeronautics, each with RON 6,000 net per month on average.

“Even though in most fields we are talking about salary increases compared with last year, in real terms employees’ purchasing power has decreased, including in the sectors where salaries increased the most, because the increases were, in most cases, even half the level of inflation. In June, the inflation rate was 10.4%,” said Roxana Drăghici, Head of Sales at eJobs, the largest online recruitment platform in Romania.

Salario data showed that employees’ expectations exceeded the salaries they received by 30% on average. The largest differences were in IT, where the salary expectations expressed by candidates were 50% higher than those offered by employers. As such, employees in this sector expected an average of RON 11,993.

The insurance sector showed differences of 42%, while the automotive industry, legal and banking sectors showed differences of 40%.

By comparison, employees in the oil and gas sector expected an average salary of RON 9,000, compared to the actual salary average, RON 7,000. In alternative medicine, the difference was only 14%, in sanitary installations 20%, and in customer relations 25%.

Data also showed that among the fields with the lowest salaries are the industries that bring the largest number of jobs to the market, namely retail, services, the food industry, and tourism. The average net salaries for these sectors were RON 4,300 for retail, RON 4,500 for the food industry, RON 4,400 for call-center/BPO, RON 5,000 for transport/logistics, and RON 5,500 for services.

The field with the lowest salaries, however, is au pair/babysitting/cleaning, with RON 3,300 per month.

According to official data, in May the average salary in the Romanian economy reached RON 5,684, up by 3.2% compared with May 2025.

World.title: Revolut opens private market funds to retail investors in Romania
World.content:
Revolut said that it launched access to private market funds for individual investors in Romania, allowing eligible customers to invest in private equity, private credit, and infrastructure assets through its app. The funds are managed by Apollo, Ares, Hamilton Lane, and Partners Group and are structured under the European Union’s ELTIF 2.0 framework.

Private market investments have traditionally been dominated by institutional investors, partly because minimum commitments can exceed EUR 100,000 and because products often involve complex documentation, capital calls, and long lock-up periods.

Revolut said the new offering is aimed at experienced investors with a long-term investment horizon and is intended to lower some of those entry barriers. Management and performance fees may apply.

The four asset managers included in the initial offering collectively manage or oversee more than USD 2.8 trillion in assets, according to the fintech company. Revolut said its internal fund selection team assesses each product’s strategy, performance history, operational resilience, and ability to withstand different market cycles.

“For a long time, private markets have been missing from the average investor’s portfolio, not because of a lack of interest, but because of a lack of access,” said Rolandas Juteika, Revolut’s head of wealth and trading for the European Economic Area. “By partnering with firms such as Apollo, Ares, Hamilton Lane, and Partners Group, we are changing that dynamic.”

The funds will use the ELTIF 2.0 structure, which was designed to broaden access to long-term investments across the EU. The products offered through Revolut will be evergreen funds, meaning investors can put money into an existing portfolio rather than waiting for capital to be deployed gradually.

However, the company warned that the investments remain fundamentally illiquid despite offering periodic redemption windows. Withdrawals are not guaranteed and may be limited or suspended under the terms of each fund.

“These funds are deliberately structured for long-term capital, reflecting the underlying nature of private assets,” Juteika said.

Revolut said investors should be prepared to hold the products for several years and should only allocate a small portion of their overall portfolio to an ELTIF.

World.title: Colombia to close embassy in Romania shortly after reopening it
World.content:
Colombia’s president-elect, Abelardo de la Espriella, announced on Sunday, July 26, that his administration, which will take office on August 7, will close at least 14 embassies, including the one in Romania, as part of a reorganization of the country’s diplomatic network.

Earlier this year, during the mandate of the current president of the South American country, Gustavo Petro, Colombia had reopened its embassy in Romania after 24 years of direct diplomatic absence between the two states.

The new president presented another course regarding the embassies. “In a first stage, I will close the embassies in Algeria, Azerbaijan, Barbados, Cuba, the Czech Republic, Ethiopia, Ghana, Haiti, Hungary, Malaysia, Nicaragua, Romania, Senegal, and South Africa,” De la Espriella said in a speech on his social media accounts in which he also announced the suspension of the opening of the mission in Palestine, according to Euronews English.

De la Espriella assured that these measures “do not mean the severing of diplomatic relations” with the affected countries, except for Cuba and Nicaragua, arguing that “there will be no link with tyrannies.”

Instead, the president-elect explained that Colombian citizens in the countries where embassies will be closed will continue to receive assistance through the concurrent representation of other diplomatic missions in the region and that the reorganization aims “to make the foreign service more efficient.”

As part of this strategy, Abelardo de la Espriella also announced the reopening of Colombia’s Embassy in Israel, which will operate in Jerusalem, a promise the new president made during the presidential campaign, and the opening of a diplomatic mission in Nigeria, to reorganize the South American country’s presence in Africa.

He also indicated that he will unify some diplomatic representations which, in his opinion, “duplicate their functions,” such as Colombia’s embassies in France and at UNESCO in Paris, as well as those in Italy and at the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in Rome, so that a single ambassador will assume both representations.

The president-elect added that within the first 100 days of his government, he will request a technical audit of the remaining diplomatic representations in order to assess their continuity and stated that the resources saved through these measures will be used to strengthen sectors such as security, health, education, and infrastructure.
