Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that his trip to Turkey will focus on investments, water, and development projects, as well as efforts to enhance stability in the region.

Turkish media highlighted the significance of the visit, as it is expected to broaden constructive collaboration between the two countries, particularly in the areas of water, energy, security, and economic cooperation, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

In addition to trade, security cooperation, and combating terrorism, al-Zaidi will discuss establishing a cooperative water management entity based on shared interests, as well as scientific collaboration and investment in advanced technology, to serve the interests of both Iraq and Turkey.

Al-Zaidi is scheduled to fly to Saudi Arabia on Thursday for an official visit, following his diplomatic trip to the Turkish capital, Ankara.

The trip is part of a larger regional diplomatic tour aiming to maintain regional balance and strengthen Iraq’s business connections.

The prime minister recently conducted high-level diplomatic visits to the United States on July 13 and Iran on July 23.

World.title: Ukraine rejects Iraqi official’s claims of Ukrainian cell operating in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Ukraine’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Tuesday dismissed statements by Iraq’s National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi, who claimed that Iraqi authorities had arrested a Ukrainian-linked cell responsible for carrying out attacks inside the country.

In an official statement, the ministry said the allegations were “groundless” and noted that no evidence had been presented to support the claims. It also pointed out that Al-Aboudi himself acknowledged during a televised interview that investigations into the matter were still ongoing.

According to the Ukrainian Foreign Ministry, Iraqi authorities did not communicate any information or concerns through diplomatic channels before the allegations were made publicly.

The ministry said that if Iraqi officials possessed credible evidence, the issue should have been raised through official diplomatic mechanisms rather than announced during a television interview. Instead, Kyiv said it first learned of the accusations through media reports.

Furthermore, Ukraine described the public remarks by a senior Iraqi official as “unacceptable and irresponsible” in the absence of supporting evidence. The ministry stressed that such statements contradict the principles of mutual respect between friendly nations and risk undermining relations between Iraq and Ukraine.

At the same time, Kyiv reaffirmed that it considers Iraq an important partner in the Middle East and remains committed to strengthening political, economic, and humanitarian cooperation between the two countries.

The Foreign Ministry also argued that the allegations mirror Russian propaganda narratives aimed at damaging Ukraine’s international reputation and weakening its partnerships across the Middle East.

Additionally, the statement suggested that the incident could have resulted from external information influence or formed part of a coordinated information campaign intended to disrupt Iraqi-Ukrainian relations.

Ukraine called on Iraqi authorities to address what it described as unfounded allegations and to prevent state institutions from promoting misinformation that could serve the interests of third parties.

The Ukrainian response follows remarks made on Monday by National Security Adviser Qasim Al-Aboudi during an interview on Dijlah TV. Al-Aboudi said Iraqi intelligence had identified what he described as Ukrainian interference inside Iraq and claimed security forces had arrested several individuals who allegedly carried out attacks on Iraqi territory.

He further stated that those detained confessed during questioning to working on behalf of Ukraine. However, Al-Aboudi did not identify the facilities allegedly targeted or specify whether the alleged operations extended beyond Iraq’s borders.

He also acknowledged that investigations into attacks carried out inside Iraq remain complex and require further examination before responsibility can be definitively assigned.

World.title: Iraqi PM expands powers as political deadlock delays cabinet completion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – A dispute over Iraq’s remaining vacant cabinet positions has expanded beyond the selection of ministers, with political factions now focusing on the growing authority of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, according to a report published by Al-Mada newspaper.

The debate follows the leak of an official document indicating that Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi has reactivated and expanded the powers of the Commander-in-Chief Office, placing several key security institutions under its supervision while the Ministries of Interior and Defense remain without permanent ministers.

According to Al-Mada, several political sources believe the expanded office significantly increases the prime minister’s direct oversight of Iraq’s security apparatus.

The report says the office now oversees the Ministries of Interior and Defense, the Counter-Terrorism Service, the National Intelligence Service, the National Security Service, the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), border crossings, military industries, and other security-related institutions.

Consequently, some political figures have described the move as a “quiet coup” against Iraq’s post-2003 political framework, arguing that it centralizes authority within the prime minister’s office while reducing the practical influence of future ministers.

Meanwhile, Iraq’s cabinet remains incomplete, with only 14 ministries currently filled while nine ministerial portfolios remain vacant. According to the report, political negotiations have become increasingly complicated, as disagreements now extend beyond candidate names to broader questions of political influence and institutional control.

Sources cited by Al-Mada said the State of Law Coalition has proposed rotating senior security positions as part of efforts to break the deadlock, particularly regarding the Interior Ministry, which traditionally falls under the Shiite political share, while the Defense Ministry is typically allocated to Sunni representatives.

However, negotiations have yet to produce a breakthrough.

At the same time, Al-Mada reported that U.S. objections have become one of the main obstacles preventing completion of the cabinet. Political sources quoted in the report claim Washington opposes appointing individuals affiliated with armed factions to ministerial positions or senior executive offices.

The report says these objections have complicated negotiations among members of the Coordination Framework, with some factions insisting that if their nominees are rejected, similar restrictions should apply to other political parties. As a result, discussions over the remaining cabinet positions have largely stalled.

Political analysts interviewed by Al-Mada argue that the continued delay in appointing ministers has allowed Prime Minister Al-Zaidi greater flexibility in managing state institutions through acting officials and appointments within his office.

According to the report, some political parties fear that prolonging the vacancies could further strengthen the prime minister’s influence over Iraq’s security establishment, making future ministerial appointments less significant.

The report also notes that recent anti-corruption campaigns and shifting political alliances have altered the balance of power within the Coordination Framework, adding another layer of complexity to negotiations.

Supporters of the government, however, argue that the current arrangements are necessary to maintain continuity while negotiations continue.

Officials quoted by Al-Mada said acting appointments and the reactivation of the Commander-in-Chief Office ensure that security institutions continue functioning despite the absence of permanent ministers.

They also expressed confidence that political forces will eventually reach an agreement to complete the cabinet, stressing that Iraq faces significant challenges, including anti-corruption efforts, security reforms, weapons control, and economic pressures linked to oil exports.

Nevertheless, the report suggests that political parties continue to use the vacant ministries as leverage in negotiations with the prime minister, making the timeline for completing the government uncertain.

World.title: Our FTAs fair & equitable, protect farmers, MSMEs, labour sector: Govt to NDA MPs
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Two Cabinet ministers have told BJP-led NDA MPs that govt has engaged in âfair, equitable and balancedâ trade agreements with large, high income and complementary economies, unlike the UPA dispensation that signed FTAs with mostly "small, competing and low per capita economies" like SAARC and ASEAN, in what is being seen as the governing allianceâs efforts to ramp up its counter to oppositionâs criticism over the issue.

At the NDA parliamentary party meeting, commerce minister Piyush Goyal and fisheries minister Lalan Singh spoke on Indiaâs free trade agreements and the growth in the fisheries sector, asserting that govt has ensured the protection of the interests of farmers, fishermen, MSMEs and the labour sector.

The FTAs under the NDA govt will be a driver of the Indian economy through global trade, Goyal's presentation said.

Indiaâs pre-2014 FTAs covered GDPs of USD 10 trillion compared to USD 60 trillion under the FTAs being entered by the NDA govt, they said.

The standout presence in the meeting, which was attended by PM Narendra Modi, was the breakaway faction of 20 TMC MPs, whose merger with Nationalist Citizens Party of India is awaiting recognition from Speaker Om Birla. Their maiden participation announced their formal entry in NDA.





Sources said the presentation on FTA (free trade agreement) at the closed door meeting accused Congress-led UPA of entering into trade deal with other countries without consulting stakeholders that ended up adversely affecting the economy.

With Rahul Gandhi repeatedly accusing govt of selling out the countryâs interests in its framework of trade agreement, whose details are still being negotiated, with the US, NDA is expected to step up its offensive, more so as the opposition may raise the issue in Parliament.

Lalan SIngh said total fish production has increased from 95.79 LT in 2013-14 to 197.75 LT in 2024 25, with the country becoming second largest fish producers with a global share of 8%. Total sea food exports have doubled from Rs 30,213 cr to Rs 62,408 cr.

"Despite US tariffs, Indiaâs seafood exports showed resilience, rising from Rs 62,408 crore in FY 2024-25 to Rs 73,890 crore in FY 2025â26 (an increase of Rs 11,482 crore)," a presentation said, adding the European Union, the UK, New Zealand, Australia, Japan, Russia, South East Asia and Middle East are emerging as new markets.

While the share of exports to the US reduced by 14% in value but it was offset by seafood exports to new markets.

Another presentation said, govt has received "committed investments" of USD 100 billions from the European Free Trade Association and USD 20 billion from New Zealand.

World.title: 'Deeply concerning': In UNSC, India strongly condemns attacks on commercial ships near Hormuz
World.content:
Ambassador Parvathaneni Harish said the recent escalation after a brief lull in fighting was deeply worrying.

NEW DELHI: India has called for an immediate de-escalation of tensions in West Asia following a fresh escalation of hostilities in the region, while strongly condemning recent attacks on commercial vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. New Delhi said attacks on civilian shipping must stop and free navigation through international waterways should be restored at the earliest.Addressing a United Nations Security Council open debate on the situation in the Middle East on Tuesday, India's permanent representative to the UN, ambassador Parvathaneni Harish, said the recent rise in violence after a brief pause in the conflict was "deeply concerning.""After a brief pause in the ongoing conflict in the region, there has been a worrying resumption of attacks and escalation of hostilities. This is deeply concerning and India calls for an immediate de-escalation of tensions," Harish said.India also strongly condemned attacks on several vessels, including GFS Galaxy, MT Al Bahiyah and MT Mombasa, during their transit through the Strait of Hormuz earlier this month.The attacks affected Indian nationals, with one Indian killed, another reported missing and several others injured, including some seriously."India has consistently condemned acts of violence targeting seafarers and disrupting free and safe navigation through international waterways like the Strait of Hormuz," Harish said.He added, "The targeting of commercial shipping and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and free and unimpeded navigation and commerce through the international waterways in the region, in keeping with international law, must be restored at the earliest."The remarks come amid the conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran. According to the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific, Iran declared the Strait of Hormuz closed again on July 11 following attacks on commercial vessels that began on July 6. Daily vessel transits, which exceeded 100 before the conflict and had recovered to 49 by July 7, fell to as low as eight to 15 by the middle of July.Harish said West Asia is a region of immense importance for India as the country's trade, energy supply chains and economic interests are closely linked to it. India has annual bilateral trade of around $180 billion with the region, cumulative foreign direct investment of more than $31 billion and receives over $52 billion in remittances from Gulf Cooperation Council countries.He also noted that around 10 million Indians live and work in the Gulf region and said, "Their safety and well-being are a key priority for us."India also urged the international community not to lose sight of the humanitarian crisis in Gaza while focusing on developments in the Strait of Hormuz."The loss of civilian lives and destruction of civilian infrastructure are pressing concerns that the international community must act on immediately, with a deep sense of urgency," Harish said.Reaffirming India's long-standing position on the Israel-Palestine issue, he said, "India believes that a sovereign, independent and viable State of Palestine living side by side in peace with Israel, within secure and recognised borders, is essential to a comprehensive and lasting solution."Harish added that India's development assistance to Palestine amounts to around $175 million.On Yemen, India reaffirmed its commitment to the country's unity, sovereignty and territorial integrity and rejected any interference in its internal affairs."We further condemn attacks by Houthis on maritime navigation. The protection of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and the Southern Red Sea is a shared international responsibility and is a global interest," Harish said.On Lebanon, India said peacekeepers serving with the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon operate under challenging circumstances and should never become targets. Harish said India strongly condemns all attacks on UNIFIL peacekeepers and added, "Further, it is important to be ready for a post-UNIFIL scenario, and in this context, the Lebanese Armed Forces must receive requisite support and assistance."

World.title: NEET has flaw in design, it is not necessary: DMK's Dayanidhi Maran
World.content:
File photo: DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran

NEW DELHI: DMK Tuesday demanded that NEET be scrapped as its MP Dayanidhi Maran in Lok Sabha asserted that the proposed amendment in the law against paper leak accused does not address the core problem bedeviling the medical entrance examination."You are not addressing the core issue. NEET is not necessary. DMK and Tamil Nadu were the first to voice their opposition to NEET due to the fundamental flaws in its design. Our warnings were never heard," he said, reiterating his party's stand against the national exam, which replaced state-level entrance tests.No longer part of the opposition INDIA bloc, Maran focused largely on his party's stand against NEET, the entrance exam to medical colleges, while tangentially referring to the recent student protest, the focus of BJP's opponents. Students have compelled parliamentarians to debate NEET, he saidHe alleged that Meta smart glasses had been used to record protesting students, following which police reached their homes. BJP grew on the back of protests, he said, asking the party as to why it was "opposed" to them.BJP is keen on getting support from DMK to push a constitution amend bill rolling out women's reservation from 2029 and raise the number of seats in Lok Sabha by over 50%.Maran claimed he and NCP - SP MP Supriya Sule were unable to use WhatsApp broadcasts for three days because of forwarding limits. "Today by mistake a Facebook post by the PM was removed, and the government called Meta chief to explain. But this is happening to MPs," Maran claimed.

World.title: Union minister, BJP MP got NHB subsidies, mantri refunded it: Government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister of state for agriculture Bhagirath Choudhary and

from Sirohi in Rajasthan Lumba Ram received financial assistance under a central scheme in 2026 and 2025, govt informed Parliament Tuesday, adding that Choudhary, however, refunded the subsidy.

In a written reply to Lok Sabha, minister of state for agriculture Ramnath Thakur said, "Bhagirath Choudhary has communicated that he has refunded the subsidy to the bank concerned under the scheme. The bank concerned has been directed to return the subsidy amount to the National Horticulture Board (NHB)".

He added, "The existing NHB scheme guidelines do not contain any specific provision regarding conflict of interest or recusal in respect of applications submitted by public functionaries or their family members."

Thakur was replying to a query by Trinamool Congress MP Abhishek Banerjee, who wanted to know whether any serving Union minister, MP or their immediate family members received subsidy under schemes of the NHB during the last five years.

Thakur said, "The NHB processes all applications for financial assistance under its schemes through a transparent mechanism... All eligible applicants are treated equally, and applications are considered solely on the basis of the eligibility criteria and compliance with the provisions of the scheme."

World.title: India slams POK elections, Pakistan's claims over Indus Valley legacy
World.content:
India slammed Pakistan for the Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (POK) polls, saying the "cosmetic electoral exercise" was just an attempt to camouflage the illegal occupation of Indian territory.

Ministry of external affairs (MEA) reiterated India's "consistent, clear and well known" position that the entire Union territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, including the areas currently under Pakistan's illegal and forcible occupation, are integral and inalienable parts of India.

"We have seen reports regarding the so-called legislative assembly elections being conducted in POK...the current cosmetic electoral exercise is nothing but an attempt by Pakistan to camouflage its illegal occupation and hide its grave human rights violations in the region," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal.

Asked about Pakistan's efforts to reclaim the Indus Valley Civilisation legacy, the official again cited Pakistan's backing of terrorism, saying a country which has been promoting cross-border terrorism, religious fundamentalism and violence for decades, cannot have any claim to any pluralistic cultural legacy.

World.title: Dealers can't keep over 400 tonne stock of sugar: Government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday issued an order capping the stock of sugar at 400 tonne with any dealer at any point of time till November 30 and traders have been directed to liquidate excess stock by August 1.

The directive, which will come into force from August 1, also says that the dealers need to sell the sweetener within 30 days from the date of receipt. Food ministry, which invoked the Essential Commodities Act to issue a gazette notification imposing restriction, said this is being done to prevent hoarding, protect consumer interests, maintain price stability and ensure a transparent and efficient sugar supply chain.

"Government has observed that the recent increase in ex-mill prices of sugar is not supported by the prevailing demand-supply fundamentals...hoarding by certain traders, dealers and market intermediaries, along with speculative transactions and paper trade without the actual physical movement of sugar from mills, has contributed to creating an artificial perception of scarcity.." the ministry said.

To keep prices under check amid a forecast of a deficit monsoon, the Centre has banned sugar exports.

The order would not apply to sugar stocks held on govt account, or by dealers nominated by the state government.

World.title: Rajya Sabha adjourned as opposition seeks Shah statement on police action
World.content:
File photo: Amit Shah

NEW DELHI: Rajya Sabha was adjourned for the day Tuesday amid repeated opposition protests demanding a statement from Union home minister Amit Shah over police action against demonstrators protesting the NEET-UG paper leak at Jantar Mantar.The House witnessed disruptions from the start of proceedings. It was first adjourned within minutes of assembling at 11am, after opposition MPs rose to raise the issue and demanded that Shah explain the police action against protesters.When RS reconvened at 2pm, deputy chairperson Harivansh attempted to take up govt's legislative business amid continued sloganeering.Union minister Jitan Ram Manjhi introduced Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill amid din. The proposed legislation was listed for introduction in the day's business. "There is a need to improve and modify the Act made in 2006," Manjhi said while introducing the bill.After its introduction, Harivansh sought to proceed to the next item - the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026 - which was listed for consideration and passage.However, Rajya Sabha could not take it up for discussion as opposition MPs continued their protest."So you don't want to run the House proceedings?" Harivansh asked the protesting MPs before adjourning the House till Wednesday.

World.title: PM Modi's message to key ministries: Be youthful, dynamic and adaptable
World.content:
File photo: PM Modi

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday told top officials of key economic ministries that govt must remain youthful and forward looking, a message that came days after he took to Instagram amid Gen Z-led protests against paper leaks."...a govt must always remain youthful, dynamic, forward-looking, continuously adapting to new challenges and opportunities with agility and innovation," PM was quoted as saying in a statement issued after his meet with secretaries and officials of ministries dealing with finance, commerce, industry and technology.He also called for the active participation of young entrepreneurs in key sectors, while asking officials to devise courses in consultation with the industry so that the workforce is equipped with skills required in emerging sectors.While education institutions have been producing a large number of engineers, professionals and graduates, often skill gap has emerged as a challenge for industry and govt's skilling initiative through the internship scheme has not had the desired impactso far.The other strong message was on addressing disinformation. "PM also emphasised the importance of proactive communication on strategic sectors where the country is undertaking major initiatives, to counter misinformation and unfounded fears surrounding such efforts," the statement said.He also underlined the need to keep citizens at the centre of every policy and decision. "Emphasising that reforms are not merely a fashionable term but a continuous necessity for effective governance, PM stressed the need to reform processes, improve work culture and strengthen institutional efficiency,"

World.title: ‘Our children may face the same struggle’: parents join Jantar Mantar protest
World.content:
NEW DELHI Worried about their children’s future and moved by Sonam Wangchuk’s deteriorating health, several parents arrived at Jantar Mantar on Friday, many with their young children in tow, as the activist entered the 20th day of his indefinite hunger strike demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over issues concerning the country’s education system.

Many of them were attending the protest, called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), for the first time and had travelled from different States. They said they decided to join after growing concerned about the deteriorating health of those on indefinite hunger strike, particularly Mr. Wangchuk. Three members of the All India Students’ Association (AISA) are also on an indefinite hunger strike. The parents appealed to those on hunger strike to call off their fast, saying the fight for reforms would be a long one.

Solidarity with protesters

Sheikh Nazim, who travelled from Jaipur with his 12-year-old son, Sheikh Fayaz, and two colleagues, sat some 200 metres from the stage on a hot and humid Friday afternoon. The four were observing a day-long fast in solidarity with Mr. Wangchuk and others on hunger strike. Their fast was scheduled to end when they reached Jaipur at midnight.

“I wanted to join the protest for a long time but could not leave my workshop in Jaipur and kept postponing it. We arrived at 7 a.m., but it took us some time to find our way around Delhi. We reached Jantar Mantar at 9 a.m.,” Mr. Nazim said.

By 2 p.m., Fayaz had stopped speaking much and responded mostly with nods, but refused to break his fast.

“My son insisted on coming with me and fasting with us because we have been following the news. Today, people are protesting over issues like the NEET paper leak and the deaths of students. My child could face similar issues one day and may have to resort to protests to exercise his right to education,” he said.

Mr. Nazim called for a better, more accountable education system and urged Mr. Wangchuk to call off his strike.

“This is going to be a long fight,” Mr. Nazim said, adding that he planned to return alone on July 20 for the CJP’s call for a march to Parliament.

Addressing supporters at the protest site, Mr. Wangchuk acknowledged his weakening physical condition but said his resolve remained unshaken.

Sarthak Gupta, who travelled with his wife and their 14-month-old child from Panipat in Haryana, said he had been following developments for several days before deciding to visit after growing concerned about Mr. Wangchuk’s health.

“We are here for two reasons — to see how Wangchuk sir is doing with our own eyes and to support the protest. If I want my child to become a better human being, he needs access to education. But given the state of our education system, he may one day have to protest himself. Seeing a great personality like Wangchuk sir in this condition feels heavy,” Mr. Gupta said.

‘Uncertain about change’

He added that he was still uncertain whether the protest would lead to change. “People like Wangchuk are fasting, and there are young people here doing the same. But will the system pay heed to us and our children? We don’t know,” he said.

For 27-year-old Jhimmil from Nagpur in Maharashtra, who stayed at the site for six hours with her five-year-old daughter, the importance of fair examinations came from experience.

“I studied in a government college because exams were fair. With paper leaks and no accountability, I don’t know what the future holds for my daughter. People have been on hunger strike over this; how can it be treated as a small issue?” she said.

She said she had hoped the government would respond before matters reached this point. “I kept thinking the protest would end, and there would be some response, but nothing has happened, so I am here today,” she said.

World.title: Vizhinjam port to handle EXIM cargo from August
World.content:
Vizhinjam port has so far served only as an international trans-shipment hub where mother ships from abroad drop off containers and pick them up. But starting August, the port will be able to handle exim cargo from and for India.

Though the arrangement comes with several caveats, businesses in Kerala and Tamil Nadu have widely welcomed the move. Being able to access an international mother ship through Vizhinjam would cut cargo transport costs by almost half, traders say.

Industry sources have said the official inauguration of exim operations will be third week of August, adding the relevant Customs notification is expected to be issued shortly.

Vizhinjam port has not been connected by road or rail for container traffic. A 2-km, six-lane road is coming up to connect to NH 66. Meanwhile, two service roads have been laid along the national highway and a trial run for container trucks conducted recently. Port officials said NHAI officials were happy with the trial run. The infrastructure for customs inspection is also available now. Only a formal notification from the Kerala government is awaited to kickstart operations.

A rail link has been planned to connect Vizhinjam to Balaramapuram along the Thiruvananthapuram-Kanniyakumari line. The 9-km rail line is scheduled to be operational when the second phase of the port is completed by 2028.

Suppliers say that for now, the port will only handle direct port entry and exit operations since there was no Container Freight Station nearby for customs clearance. But the start of operations itself is a positive sign and could soon lead to full-fledged exim handling by the port.

World.title: This Gandhi accepts GPay: Meet Marina Beach’s living Mahatma
World.content:
The Marina Beach in Chennai comes alive on weekends. Even as the smells of sundal and bajji waft through the air, eager children pester parents so they can ride a horse, or shoot balloons. Others prefer to silently gaze at the sea or the statues.

Not too far from the landmark Gandhi Statue at this beach stands another statue - except this one moves occasionally. Meet Nehemia Koche, who is now 68. He is a regular these days to the beach during weekend evenings, but he cannot afford to indulge in bajjis or games.

That is because Nehemia Koche is Gandhi. Using silver body paint, which he applies for about half hour, Nehemia arrives at the Marina Beach every weekend and stands. He is mostly as still as a statue, but he does occasionally stretch his legs or salute the curious passers-by.

“People have forgotten Gandhiji. This is my way of reminding them about the father of the nation,” he says, taking a stroll after a tiring few hours of standing.

In that time, this street artiste has earned around 600 rupees. “It [the money I earn] depends on the number of people who visit the beach,” says Nehemia, who usually stands at the beach opposite the Public Works Department building, “Children love me and are usually excited to take pictures. Sometimes, they even want to touch me to see if I am real!” The adults, however, are more sober. “While some just shake hands with me and go away, some are interested in selfies. A few of them donate some money in the box that I keep. Sometimes, they give me food too.”

Interestingly, Nehemia also has a QR code attached to his trousers, keeping with today’s times of digital transactions. “I have to find new ways of making ends meet. Back home, I have a 27-year-old daughter who wishes to start earning before she gets married. I am saving up for her future.”

Play it up

Hailing from China Munagala village in Khammam district (Telangana), this street artiste has been performing and dressing up as the Mahatma for many years now. “Right from childhood, I have been interested in street theatre and plays. Whenever there was a festive occasion in our village, I would dress up as a character and attend the celebrations. I have also dressed up as lord Ram during temple festivities. Dressing up as a famous character has been a habit for me, especially during Sankaranthi and Ugadi,” he adds.

Over time, this act also started fetching him money, food and shelter. “I have travelled widely across India to popular tourist spots, especially the beaches of Mumbai and Vishakakapatnam. The Marina Beach at Madras is one of my favourite places to come to — because people here are friendly. Even the policemen treat me with respect; they sometimes give me food packets.” Apart from beaches, he has also visited educational institutions in Warangal and Vishakapatnam dressed as Gandhi.

On August 15 this year, even as India celebrates its Independence Day, Nehemia will be back at his regular haunt on Marina Beach. As the beach comes alive with Independence Day celebrations, Gandhi will take a stroll.

World.title: Kanchi Kamakoti CHILDS Trust Hospital launchesclinic for cystic fibrosis
World.content:
:

Kanchi Kamakoti CHILDS Trust Hospital in Chennai, has launched a dedicated multi-disciplinary clinic for cystic fibrosis, in order to bring together diagnosis, treatment and long-term management for children under one roof.

Explaining the challenges involved with cystic fibrosis, which is a genetic disorder that causes thick mucus to build up in the body and affect multiple organs, Janani Sankar, medical director, KKCTH, at a press meet on Thursday said children presented with different symptoms, including recurrent lung infections, oily stools, and inadequate weight gain, which often led to difficulties in early diagnosis.

Having to go to multiple specialists at different centres also took a physical, emotional, and financial toll on families, she said.

Bala Ramachandran, head of paediatric intensive care, noted that cystic fibrosis was estimated to be present in 1 in 10,000 live births in India and that many more children were likely living with it undiagnosed.

He explained that the condition not only affected the lungs, but could also cause nutritional deficiencies, diabetes, and other complications.

Stressing that early diagnosis was key to preserve lung function, he said paediatric interventional pulmonology, endocrinology, as well as gastrointestinal, nutritional and psychological care were required, and that the best outcomes were seen when all services were in one place, making treatment compliance easier for patients and families.

V.V. Vivekananad, consultant pulmonologist, said the hospital was now offering advances paediatric interventional pulmonology services, including endobronchial ultrasounds and bronchoscopic cryotherapy services. These interventions allowed for children to avoid invasive surgeries and quickened their recovery times, he said.

The clinic will function on the second Saturday of every month.

The hospital is also conducting a continuing medical education programme on July 19, bringing together paediatricians and specialists to discuss recent advances in diagnosis and management, to build awareness, and promote early diagnosis.

World.title: What is the EU AI transparency code? | Explained
World.content:
The European Union is set to make labelling of AI-generated content mandatory from August 2, in a move to ensure transparency and enable human users to distinguish manipulated content online. Falling under the purview of Article 50 of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AIA), which sets a framework for the use and supply of AI systems within the bloc with a risk-based categorisation, the ‘Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content’ stipulates certain obligation for AI developers and providers to maintain the integrity of the information ecosystem, with administrative fines up to €15 million for non-compliance.

What are the contents that need to be labeled under the new code?

The European Commission has summarised the scope of the transparency code into two broad categories of online content: deepfakes and manipulated text. Deepfakes refer to images, audio, or video resembling existing persons, places, or events that are generated (or manipulated) with AI and would appear to a human user as authentic. Manipulated text includes that published to pass information to the public that has not undergone human review. The code requires AI system developers and content providers to display prominent, distinguishable signs that such products are artificial.

What are the exceptions to the new code?

While the code seeks to make digital spaces trustworthy for human users, it has given certain leeway for the use of AI, especially for creative content. For deepfakes that are part of products that are evidently artistic, satirical, or fictional, the code has simplified transparency obligations, stipulating appropriate disclosure without hampering the display of the work. The disclosure obligation is also done away with for content “authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate, or prosecute criminal offences”. AI-generated text that has undergone human review or is under editorial control with a legally liable person holding responsibility for it, is also exempt from the obligation.

How should an AI-generated content be labeled under the code?

The EU has listed out three kinds of icons to be displayed with deepfakes and manipulated text for compliance with the AIA: a basic ‘AI’ icon if the technology merely involved in the creation of a product; an ‘AI generated’ icon for those entirely produced by the technology with no human element involved except prompts; and an ‘AI modified’ icon for pre-existing, human-made content that has undergone manipulation with AI tools.

How is the EU code different from regulations in India?

The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, in February this year, notified an amendment to the IT Rules, 2021, that required users and social media platforms to label synthetically generated information (SGI) prominently for users to see. However, while the EU code requires developers of AI systems to include the label, India puts focus on social media, with the onus on users for the disclosure while relying on the platforms to enforce it. While the EU code seeks to bring about accountability from AI systems to improve responsible content generation, India has sought to regulate the final product with provisions for platforms to take down content that goes against the IT Rules. Also, the EU has laid down specific exemptions for creative content and put trust on human review, Indian rules are more generic and don’t provide such leeway.

How have industry leaders responded to the new requirements?

While most of the leading AI companies have signed on to the initiative, some have expressed reservations. While Google has also signed on to the code and noted that the initiative goes with its work to develop AI transparency tools, it is concerned about the regulatory complexity of the code. “If online content is flooded with overlapping AI labels and legal disclosures, it becomes harder for people to get the clear context they need”, Karen Massin, Google’s head of Government Affairs and Public Policy — EU Institutions, said in a statement. “Adding more regulatory complexity — as technical solutions are still evolving — could contradict Europe’s goals for competitiveness and simplification”, the statement said, adding that “it also risks confusing the people these rules are meant to help”. OpenAI has also welcomed the code and extended support to it, saying that it is “committed to doing our part by complying with the requirements that apply to our relevant products”. As AI tools become a part of how people build, imagine, and share, it’s important that people can understand where content comes from and interpret it with confidence, it said. However, the AI giant has acknowledged that the transparency push is still a nascent field as icons can be tampered with, and metadata can be removed. Saying that advancing the reliability of such techniques requires significant work among the AI ecosystem, it has called for the new code to be grounded in methods that are flexible enough to reflect limitations of current techniques.

World.title: Congress and ‘Cockroach’ supporters attempting to create anarchy in the country, says BJP MLA V. Sunil Kumar
World.content:
Former Minister V. Sunil Kumar on Tuesday, alleged that some people are attempting to create anarchy in the country in the name of some movement and are inciting the young generation in the name of ‘Cockroach’.

Mr. Kumar was speaking at a protest organised by the Udupi district unit of Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) at the Jatka Stand in Udupi alleging that ‘Cockroaches’ and Congress supporters were creating anarchy in the country and following a goonda culture and anti-national policies.

Mr. Kumar said the protest by ‘Cockroaches’ in the name of NEET examination paper leak was an attempt to insult the country by using abusive words against Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Hinduism. He said no government has justified the NEET question paper leak. Re-examination was conducted as soon as the issue came to light. However, he said, attempts were being made to create a vicious atmosphere against the country by using such incidents as a pretext.

The Karkala MLA said during the tenure of Mr. Modi, India’s standing at the international level has increased. However, some forces were working to weaken the country. He criticised the Congress for not having faith in the electoral system, Parliament and the law.

Mr. Kumar said there was a need to create awareness among the people about anti-social and anti-national activities that involve collaboration with foreign forces.

He alleged that when the Citizenship Amendment Act was being implemented, Congress utilised the opportunity to incite Muslims against the country. It also questioned the operations of the Indian Defence forces during the surgical strikes and ‘Operation Sindoor.’ He alleged that people with similar mindsets were now protesting in the name of ‘Cockroaches.’

Indian society does not accept stone-pelting on soldiers and attacks on police in the name of movement.

Other BJP MLAs from the district, Gururaj Gantihole, A. Kiran Kumar Kodgi, Yashpal Suvarna and Gurme Suresh Shetty, District BJP President Kutyar Naveen Shetty and others were present.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 8 LIVE: Opposition MPs move notices in Parliament over Anti-Defection Law reform, Cauvery water dispute
World.content:
Ahead of the parliamentary proceedings on Wednesday (July 29, 2026), Opposition members from both the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha have submitted notices to suspend regular business to discuss issues ranging from electoral reforms to inter-State water disputes.

In the Lok Sabha, Congress MP Manish Tewari gave a notice for an adjournment motion, seeking a comprehensive discussion on the necessity of a new Anti-Defection Law. Mr. Tewari argued that the current legal framework needs an overhaul to prevent mass floor-crossing driven by political opportunism.

Also Read: Why Tamil Nadu and Karnataka are sparring over Cauvery water? | Explained

Ending a week-long logjam, the Lok Sabha on Tuesday (July 28, 2026) debated on the Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.

World.title: RSS distances itself from Hindutva ideologue T.G. Mohandas’s controversial remarks on Jantar Mantar protestors
World.content:
The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has condemned the controversial remarks made by Hindutva ideologue T.G. Mohandas against the student protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi that culminated in the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

In a video posted on his YouTube channel on July 26, Mr. Mohandas had threatened that he “would have shot” the protestors at Jantar Mantar if he were in control. A former head of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)’s State intellectual cell, he had said in another video that secular women who take part in protests “enjoy being gangraped.”

K. B. Sreekumar, Saha Prantha Karyavah (South Kerala) of the RSS, said in a statement that Mr. Mohandas’s comments on the protests are “his personal thoughts and he is not an RSS official at any level.” Mr. Sreekumar said the organisation does not agree with his views and “such views should be condemned in every highest possible manner”.

In a 30-minute video, Mr. Mohandas spoke at length about how he would have tackled the student protests by the CJP and other major Opposition outfits against the NEET exam irregularities. “I will impose a curfew in about a 4 square kilometre area around Jantar Mantar. Then I would announce thrice for the crowd to disperse. After that, I will open fire. People will scatter away and run for their lives. Some may die, some may suffer disabilities. Within four hours, the situation will be calm. Then I will collect the bodies and take them to hospitals,” he said.

“Gangrapes will happen. In this case, there won’t be any complaints as these are people who like being raped. There are women who like being raped, especially Leftists, secular, democratic and proletarians. Now if someone dies during this, they will turn the person into a martyr,” he said.

Kerala’s Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala had ordered a police investigation against the controversial remarks made by Mr. Mohandas. The probe was initiated following complaints lodged by the representatives of the All India Youth Federation (AIYF), Sudents’ Federation of India (SFI), Youth Congress and the People’s Democratic Party. He had directed P. Prakash, Inspector General of Police, to carry out an investigation.

Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan had demanded that the government should register a case against Mr. Mohandas while pointing out that his controversial statements “reflected the Sangh Parivar’s desire to curb dissent.”

Mohandas says remarks 'satirical, hypothetical’

After his statements invited widespread protests, Mr. Mohandas clarified that his remarks were intended to be “satirical” and “hypothetical”. He alleged that short clips of his comments were taken out of context.

World.title: Delhi Police files FIR over abusive posts against PM Modi, seeks details from X
World.content:
Delhi Police has filed an FIR regarding abusive social media posts against PM Modi and asked X to provide details about account posted the videos. The FIR was filed over a complaint that “derogatory, malicious and defamatory content is being circulated on social media platform targeting constitutional heads”.

The Delhi Police has asked X (formerly Twitter) to delete and remove the alleged post or video from the platform immediately. It has also sought the full details, such as full name, address, contact details and email ID of the owner of the X account, from which the content was posted. This includes the login and logout details with time and date stamp.

World.title: Consider paid menstrual leave for KSRTC women conductors: Kerala High Court
World.content:
Calling menstrual leave a “progressive welfare measure” that recognises the physical and psychological impact of menstruation, the Kerala High Court has asked the state government to consider introducing a menstrual leave policy for Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) women conductors, saying the physically demanding nature of their work warrants such a measure.

Justice Viju Abraham was hearing a writ petition filed by three women conductors employed by the KSRTC, along with the Forum for Justice (FFJ), a welfare organisation for KSRTC employees and their families. The petition sought directions to the state government and KSRTC to consider a representation seeking two days’ paid menstrual leave for women conductors.

“Menstrual leave is a progressive welfare measure that recognises the physical and psychological impact of menstruation on women employees. It is consistent with Articles 21, 15(3) and Article 42 of the Constitution of India, which collectively support the protection of women’s dignity and the provision of just and humane working conditions,” the court said on July 23.

The petition highlighted that women conductors routinely work long shifts, often between eight and sixteen hours, spending most of the day on their feet while navigating crowded buses to issue tickets and collect fares. It also pointed to the lack of hygienic toilets, adequate rest areas and proper menstrual waste disposal facilities across many KSRTC depots, arguing that these conditions make menstruation particularly difficult for women employees.

Justice Viju Abraham said that a limited provision for menstrual leave would promote employee welfare, enhance productivity, and foster a more inclusive workplace. (Image enhanced using AI) Justice Viju Abraham said that a limited provision for menstrual leave would promote employee welfare, enhance productivity, and foster a more inclusive workplace. (Image enhanced using AI)

Conductors approached court

The petitioners told the high court that women conductors face significant physical and emotional challenges during menstruation because of prolonged duty hours, continuous movement and inadequate workplace facilities.

According to the plea, nearly 3,000 women employees work in KSRTC’s operating sector. However, many depots lack clean toilets with water, sufficient resting spaces and proper disposal systems for menstrual hygiene products, leading to discomfort and health concerns during working hours.

The petitioners submitted a representation to the Kerala government on October 30, 2025, requesting the introduction of a menstrual leave policy for women employees in KSRTC. Since no decision had been taken on the representation, they moved the high court seeking appropriate directions.



Dignity, policy

Recognising the nature of the work performed by women conductors, Justice Abraham observed that menstrual leave is consistent with constitutional guarantees protecting women’s dignity and welfare.

The court noted that KSRTC women conductors perform physically demanding duties involving prolonged standing, continuous movement, long working hours and limited access to hygienic restroom facilities.

It further observed that severe menstrual symptoms may substantially affect their health, dignity and ability to discharge their duties efficiently.

“A limited provision for menstrual leave would promote employee welfare, reduce presenteeism, enhance productivity, and foster a more inclusive workplace,” the court said.

The high court observed that, given the working conditions of women conductors, the state government could examine introducing an appropriate menstrual leave policy.

“In view of the nature of their duties and working conditions, the Government may consider introducing an appropriate policy providing menstrual leave to women conductors, subject to such conditions and safeguards as may be deemed appropriate,” the judgment said.

However, instead of directing the government to frame such a policy, the court ordered the state to consider and decide the petitioners’ pending representation within three months after giving an opportunity of hearing to both the petitioners and KSRTC.

Measures adopted elsewhere

The petitioners informed the court that the Karnataka government had announced one day’s paid menstrual leave every month for women aged 18 to 52 working in both government and private sectors in November 2025. They also referred to menstrual leave policies in Bihar and Odisha.

The plea further pointed out that Kerala has already introduced menstrual leave for women students in several universities, but similar benefits have not yet been extended to women government employees or KSRTC staff.

World.title: Kerala man orders Rs 359 earbuds gets ‘wrong’ brand, wins Rs 8,359 payout
World.content:
The commission was hearing a complaint filed by a man who ordered the earbuds in April 2025 from a Gurugram-based online marketplace, Vle Bazaar. (AI-generated image)

A Kerala consumer commission has found an online marketplace guilty of deficiency in service after a man was delivered BoAT earbuds instead of his choice of brand, WeCool, and ordered a Rs 8,359 payout.

President D B Binu, along with members Ramachandran V and Sreevidhia T N, was hearing the complaint filed by one Santosh who ordered the earbuds in April 2025 from a Gurugram-based online marketplace, Vle Bazaar.

“The intentional non-appearance of the opposite party (Vle Bazaar) and non-participation in the proceedings of the Commission even after receiving the notice sent from the commission very clearly shows that the opposite party has nothing to offer against the allegations of the complaint, which amounts to admission of the statements made by the complainant,” the July 14 order read.

World.title: After India coaching exit, Ryan ten Doeschate joins KKR as Strategy Head
World.content:
Just weeks before India’s Test tour to Sri Lanka, assistant coach Ryan ten Doeschate vacated his post to join former Indian Premier League (IPL) champions Kolkata Knight Riders on Wednesday. The three-time IPL winners announced Ten Doeschate’s appointment as their new Head of Cricket Strategy.

“In his new role, Ryan will lead the strategic direction for scouting, player recruitment, squad planning and performance evaluation across the Knight Riders network. He will work closely with the coaching teams to help build a consistent cricketing philosophy and approach across all Knight Riders franchises. As part of his role, he will also serve as Assistant Coach for Trinbago Knight Riders in the CPL, Abu Dhabi Knight Riders in the ILT20 and Los Angeles Knight Riders in the MLC,” KKR said in its statement.

World.title: Harshad Chopda, Shreya Kalra recall childhood abuse on Lock Upp: ‘99% kids go through it’
World.content:
This week on Lock Upp: Sach Ya Sazaa has been an emotional one for the contestants. After Shilpa Shinde and Ram Kapoor revealed their secrets for the weekly budget task, Harshad Chopda and Shreya Kalra also shared traumatic incidents from their childhood. In the latest episode, both contestants spoke about surviving childhood sexual abuse, leaving fellow contestants Ram Kapoor and Shivangi Joshi visibly emotional. Shreya also said she had long kept her experience private because she feared it could affect her family.

On the Farah Khan-Riteish Deshmukh-hosted show, Harshad had already revealed his two secrets. And in the latest episode, he gave out the third and last one too. Getting emotional, Harshad shared, “I was 9 or 10 years old. Parents sometimes trust people and leave their kids with them. Once my parents also did that; they left me with some trusted people. I was a submissive kid. At night, somebody was rubbing himself on me. While the clothes were on, I was lying down, and somebody was on top of me. I didn’t know what was happening; I was scared, so I acted like I was sleeping. No one knows this.”

Also Read: ‘Scars are still there’: Harshad Chopda opens up about painful past on Lock Upp 2

Harshad was harrassed by a gay at the age of 9 . Everyone judged him when he made some remarks about gay . This is the reason why he feels uncomfortable around gay .#HarshadChopda #LockUpp2 pic.twitter.com/ljPaJbXlx7 — 𝑨𝒗𝒚𝒂𝒂𝒏🦭 (@avyyaan) July 28, 2026

Harshad said the incident has left him fearful.

“He once called me to the balcony on the pretext of showing me something; he lifted me, and again did something. I didn’t question it because I was scared. I just want to request all parents: don’t leave your kids anywhere, and speak to them regularly so that they can share feelings with you. For people like me, we should always inform parents about it, so that the abusers are called out. Those people are still around, hale and hearty, and I am here with my fear. Because of this, even though I don’t hate gay men, I am scared of them,” Harshad added.

Learning about Harshad’s story, Ram Kapoor cried and said, “All parents should listen to this. This is so common; boys are abused as much as girls.” A few weeks back, Ram had also opened up about facing sexual abuse as a child. Shivangi Joshi also got emotional and said, “This is so disgusting, but it’s so common.”

While talking to her and Akanksha Chamola, Harshad Chopda added, “99 percent of kids go through this. We are the future parents, and we will stop it. Just imagine, you went through something, and you are unaware of it. So you are not really harmed or scarred like that.” Akanksha Chamola added, “It’s not about being physically harmed; it is the mental and emotional harm which is worse than physical scars.”

Shreya Kalra recalls abuse by a cousin

Shreya Kalra also got very emotional as she shared her secret. She said, “I wanted to protect my secrets not because I want to go in the finale, but because it can ruin a lot of things in my family. I have been molested by one of my cousins. Only my boyfriend knows about this. I was 13; I used to go to my grandmother’s house, where we slept in the living room. This cousin, who was 3-4 years older than me, would grab me; I didn’t know what was even going on.”

Shreya’s secret: “I was molested by one of my cousins when I was 13 years old. Until now, only Rishabh knew about it.” 💔 Bro, this is literally heartbreaking. Stay strong, Shreya. 💔 This is just unbelievable.#ShreyaKalra #LockUpp2 #LockUpp pic.twitter.com/xHJREKFjfq — Digital News Hub (@digital_newshub) July 28, 2026

“I would be the last person to victimize myself. I didn’t want my mother to know this, because the guy who did this had lost his mother, and my mother took care of him for almost three years. Also, my real brother is getting married in November, and his previous engagement broke off because of me. I didn’t want this to come out; I blame myself to date for his engagement being called off because I was in this industry and had some controversies. Finally, he is getting married and has a chance to be happy, and I think I am going to ruin it again,” Shreya Kalra added.



“Honestly, I don’t even know why it happened with me. I feel bad that while I fight to stand up for myself, I couldn’t expose him ever. I went to attend that cousin’s wedding with my family. My mom will break down hearing this,” Shreya concluded.

Lock Upp: Sach Ya Sazaa will conclude with its grand finale on August 5. The show streams on Netflix India every day at 8 pm.

World.title: India’s HIV fight has changed: Why ageing, diabetes and new hotspots are the next big challenge
World.content:
India’s HIV programme is often held up as a public health success story. New infections and AIDS-related deaths have fallen sharply over the past decade, millions of people are receiving life-saving antiretroviral therapy and viral suppression rates are among the highest in the world. But as people with HIV live longer, the country’s battle against the epidemic is entering a new phase.

Doctors are now grappling with an ageing population living with HIV, many of whom are developing diabetes, hypertension, heart disease and other non-communicable diseases that require integrated care. At the same time, fresh HIV transmission hotspots linked to injecting drug use have emerged in states such as Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura and Punjab, underscoring that the epidemic continues to evolve.

Dr Sanjay Pujari, Director and Chief Consultant at the Institute of Infectious Diseases, Pune, will be speaking on clinical strategies for integrating HIV, tuberculosis (TB) and non-communicable diseases at the International AIDS Conference being held in Rio de Janeiro. He spoke to The Indian Express about India’s changing HIV landscape, the country’s role in the global response and the priorities for ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.



What is the current burden of HIV in the country, and what concerns you the most?

India’s HIV response has come a long way. By the end of 2023, an estimated 2.54 million people were living with HIV, with an adult prevalence of 0.20%. Over the past decade, we’ve seen encouraging progress; new HIV infections have fallen by 44.2% since 2010, while AIDS-related deaths have dropped by 79.2%. Today, around 1.8 million people receive free antiretroviral therapy (ART) through the national programme, with 94% treatment retention and 97% viral suppression, which is a significant public health achievement.

But success brings a new set of challenges. Because people with HIV are living longer, we’re now seeing more of them develop age-related conditions such as diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular disease. The proportion of people living with HIV, who are over 50, has risen from 17% in 2000 to 37% in 2023, and is expected to cross 50% by 2030. This means our focus must shift from treating HIV alone to managing HIV alongside other chronic illnesses. Another area of concern is the emergence of HIV transmission hotspots in states such as Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Tripura and Punjab, where infections are being driven largely by needle sharing among people who inject drugs.



What unique perspective does India bring to this year’s global HIV agenda?

India’s experience shows that a nationally owned and predominantly domestically-funded HIV programme can be both sustainable and resilient. At a time when many countries are grappling with shrinking international support, that is an important lesson for the global HIV community.

The second major contribution is India’s role as the pharmacy of the world for HIV medicines. Nearly 80% of the antiretroviral drugs used globally are manufactured by Indian pharmaceutical companies. As discussions increasingly turn to equitable access to treatment and newer prevention tools, India’s manufacturing capacity becomes even more critical. The same is likely to hold true for innovations such as long-acting injectable prevention medicines like lenacapavir.

How is India incorporating newer HIV prevention strategies, such as long-acting PrEP (pre-exposure prophylaxis) into its public health programme?



India already has national guidelines for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) but access to these medicines has not yet been expanded as part of a large-scale public health programme.

One of the most exciting developments in HIV prevention is lenacapavir, a long-acting injectable that offers protection with just one injection every six months. It has not yet been approved by Indian regulators because additional country-specific safety and efficacy data are needed. However, Gilead Sciences has already signed voluntary, royalty-free licensing agreements with four Indian generic manufacturers. Once regulatory approval is granted, lenacapavir could become a valuable addition to India’s HIV prevention strategy.

Does stigma and discrimination continue to affect people living with HIV?

The situation has improved considerably over the years, but stigma has certainly not disappeared. Many people living with HIV continue to struggle with internalised stigma, which calls for sustained counselling and psychosocial support. At the same time, discrimination still exists within families, communities and, unfortunately, even in some healthcare settings.



Health insurance is one area where significant gaps remain. People living with HIV are often denied adequate insurance coverage despite advances in treatment that allow them to lead long and productive lives.

India has an important legal safeguard in the HIV and AIDS (Prevention and Control) Act, 2017, which prohibits discrimination in employment, healthcare, education and other areas. The challenge now is ensuring that these protections translate into meaningful change on the ground.

Looking ahead to 2030, what do you see as the biggest opportunity—and the biggest challenge—in ending HIV as a public health threat in India?

As people living with HIV age, healthcare must evolve with their needs. We need models that integrate HIV care with the management of diabetes, cardiovascular disease and other chronic conditions. While there have been examples of programme-level integration, the next step is to develop standardised clinical pathways so that care is organised around the individual rather than around separate diseases.



The biggest opportunity lies in India’s generic pharmaceutical industry, which is well placed to shape the future of the global HIV response by making both affordable treatment and long-acting preventive medicines more widely available. At the same time, if India is to achieve its goal of ending AIDS as a public health threat by 2030, it will need to sharpen its focus on prevention and treatment in the geographic hotspots where HIV prevalence remains higher than the national average.

As international HIV funding becomes more constrained, how should India adapt its HIV response?

Fortunately, India is less vulnerable to international funding cuts than many other countries. According to UNAIDS, we have relatively low dependence on PEPFAR funding and are grouped with countries such as South Africa, Thailand and Brazil.

That doesn’t mean funding reductions will have no impact. Community-based organisations and research projects supported by the US government and the National Institutes of Health (NIH) could face disruptions, which may affect some services and ongoing research. However, the national HIV programme itself is built largely on domestic funding, making it far more resilient to these global financial shifts.

World.title: Jharkhand’s top Maoist leader Misir Besra, carrying Rs 1 crore bounty, arrested
World.content:
Misir Besra entered the Maoist movement in the mid-1980s, rose through the ranks over nearly four decades and played a key role in building the outfit's organisational and armed structure in Jharkhand. (File photo)

Misir Besra, the only remaining senior Maoist leader operating in Jharkhand and a CPI (Maoist) politburo member carrying a Rs 1 crore bounty, was arrested on Tuesday near Dhanbad along with two other Maoists and two villagers, senior officials said.

The other Maoists arrested are Tumba Manjhi, a regional committee member, and Biren Hansda, an area committee member of the CPI (Maoist).

According to the police, acting on specific intelligence inputs, the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) and its Commando Battalion for Resolute Action (CoBRA) unit jointly planned and executed the operation after receiving information that Besra, 65, was present in the forested area straddling Dhanbad and Giridih districts.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session 2026 Day 8 Live Updates: Anti exam-paper leak law to be presented today
World.content:
Lok Sabha proceedings underway during the Monsoon Session of Parliament in New Delhi. (Source: PTI)

On the 8th day of Parliament Monsoon session, MPs are expected to discuss and pass the strict new law to curb exam paper leaks offered as a solution by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to address the month-long students’ protest that have spawned a huge challenge to his 12-year tenure. The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill 2026 will be presented by Union Minister Jitendra Singh on Wednesday. It seeks to amend the 2024 anti-paper leak law to strengthen measures against paper leak. Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is expected to speak around 2 pm today.

Parliament is also expected to take the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill 2026, with Union Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal set to move the legislation for consideration and passage on Wednesday. Besides that, several ministers will table official papers related to their ministries, while the House is slated to consider a motion seeking more time for the Joint Parliamentary Committee to submit its report on the One Nation, One Election Bills until the Winter Session of 2026.
